classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate
items.description:
Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical
dissipation of fluid momentum for a specified ion charge state, expressed as
a vector whose components quantify the damping rate along distinct geometric
projections.
items.documentation:
The ion charge state momentum damping rate is the effective inverse
relaxation timescale at which ordered fluid momentum of a specified ion
charge state is dissipated through Coulomb collisions and neoclassical
viscous stresses. As a vector, it encodes the direction-dependent damping
coefficient along the radial, poloidal, toroidal, and field-parallel
geometric projections.

The defining relation for a fluid momentum density component $p_s$ of ion
charge state $s$ subject to dissipation is:

$$
\frac{\partial p_s}{\partial t}\bigg|_{\rm damp} = -\nu_{D,s} \, p_s
$$

where $\nu_{D,s}$ is the charge-state damping rate and $p_s$ is the directed
fluid momentum density of the specified charge state. The magnitude of
$\nu_{D,s}$ is set by Coulomb collisionality, the charge-state mass and
effective charge number, and the local magnetic geometry through
neoclassical friction-force coefficients.

This quantity resolves the general
[momentum_damping_rate](name:momentum_damping_rate) at the level of an
individual ion charge state, in contrast to
[ion_momentum_damping_rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate), which
represents the charge-state-aggregated ion population. Scalar projections
along each geometric direction include
[parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate)
for the field-aligned component.

items.name: fast_neutron_flux_of_correction_coil
items.description:
Incident crossing rate of fast neutrons per unit area on the inboard-facing
surface of a non-axisymmetric correction coil.
items.documentation:
Fast neutron number flux is the incident crossing rate of the fast-neutron
population per unit area on the inboard-facing surface of a non-axisymmetric
correction coil. It is the fast-neutron component of neutron flux of
correction coil.

The differential number flux is defined by

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{fast}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{fast}}}{dA\,dt}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the number of fast neutrons incident on surface
area $A$ and $t$ is time; $A$ is measured in m$^2$ and $t$ in s.

The inboard-facing surface is the side directed toward decreasing major
radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This
quantity includes only incident fast-neutron crossings and excludes outgoing
crossings and the energy-integrated neutron flux.

items.name: flux_due_to_surface_emission
items.description:
Flux of any physical quantity emanating from a material surface through
emission processes such as particle recycling, sputtering, or secondary
electron and photon emission.
items.documentation:
Surface emission encompasses the range of physical processes by which
plasma-facing material surfaces re-emit particles, energy, or radiation into
the plasma or surrounding environment. These include neutral recycling
(incident ions reflected or thermally desorbed as neutrals), physical and
chemical sputtering (wall atoms ejected by energetic ion bombardment),
secondary electron emission (electrons liberated by ion or electron impact),
and thermal or fluorescence photon emission from heated or excited surface
atoms.

The emitted flux $\Gamma_\mathrm{emit}$ at a surface element is related to
the incident driving flux $\Gamma_\mathrm{incident}$ through a
process-specific emission yield $Y$:

$$
\Gamma_\mathrm{emit} = Y \cdot \Gamma_\mathrm{incident}
$$

where $Y$ is the emission yield (dimensionless for particle emission, or
carrying the appropriate units ratio for energy or photon emission), and
$\Gamma_\mathrm{incident}$ is the incident flux of the driving species.

The specific instantiation of this flux at the first wall is described by
[flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission).
For the total radiated thermal power emitted by wall material, see
thermal_power_of_wall_material_due_to_radiation_emission. General energy
transport through a surface is captured by energy_flux.

items.name: voltage_amplitude_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
items.description:
Peak magnitude of the radio-frequency voltage waveform on a single
transmission-line feed of an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the peak magnitude of the radio-frequency electrical
potential difference on one transmission-line feed belonging to an
ion-cyclotron-heating antenna module.

For the feed voltage waveform $v(t)$, its amplitude is defined by

$$
V_{\mathrm{amp}} = \max_t |v(t)|
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{amp}}$ is the voltage amplitude, $v(t)$ is the
instantaneous feed voltage, and $t$ is time. The absolute value removes
instantaneous polarity, while the maximum selects the peak magnitude of the
waveform.

The quantity applies to one feed of one antenna module and is not a sum over
feeds, antenna modules, or the complete heating system. It excludes the
instantaneous signed voltage and its phase; it also does not represent
forward or launched radio-frequency power. It is the amplitude
transformation of the corresponding [ion-cyclotron-heating antenna
voltage](name:voltage_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), retaining the feed
voltage's peak level while discarding its instantaneous sign and phase.

items.name: perpendicular_runaway_electron_convection_velocity
items.description:
Signed cross-field component of the effective runaway-electron convection
velocity, projected along the outward normal to nested magnetic flux
surfaces.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the directed transport velocity of runaway electrons across
magnetic flux surfaces, isolated from the field-aligned component of the
[runaway-electron convection
velocity](name:runaway_electron_convection_velocity).

The perpendicular component is defined by

$$
v_{\perp}^{\rm RE} = \mathbf{v}_{\rm RE} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\psi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\rm RE}$ is the effective runaway-electron
convection-velocity vector and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\psi}$ is the outward unit
normal to nested magnetic flux surfaces. This convective quantity describes
directed cross-field transport and excludes diffusive spreading, which is
characterized by the [perpendicular runaway-electron
diffusivity](name:perpendicular_runaway_electron_diffusivity). It
contributes to the [perpendicular runaway-electron particle
flux](name:perpendicular_runaway_electron_particle_flux) together with the
runaway-electron density.

Sign convention: Positive when runaway-electron convection is directed
outward from the magnetic axis toward increasing flux label.

items.name: rotation_frequency_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode
items.description:
Instantaneous angular rate of phase evolution of an individual neoclassical
tearing mode, with its sign distinguishing phase advance from phase
regression.
items.documentation:
The angular rotation frequency of a neoclassical tearing mode is the
instantaneous signed rate at which its phase changes. It applies to an
individual mode, without averaging over modes or over a time interval.

The defining relation is:

$$
\omega_{\mathrm{NTM}}(t) = \frac{d\Phi_{\mathrm{NTM}}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $\omega_{\mathrm{NTM}}$ is the mode's angular rotation frequency,
$\Phi_{\mathrm{NTM}}$ is its [phase](name:neoclassical_tearing_mode_phase),
followed continuously across complete turns, and $t$ is time.

This quantity describes mode-pattern phase motion, not the material angular
velocity of the plasma. It is distinct from the [cyclic rotation
frequency](name:frequency_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode): when both refer to
the same rotation phase, the angular rate equals $2\pi$ times the cyclic
rate. Its time derivative is the [angular acceleration of the
mode](name:rotation_frequency_time_derivative_of_neoclassical_tearing_mode),
not the rotation frequency itself.

Sign convention: Positive when the continuously followed mode phase
increases with time.

items.name: neutral_state_power_density
items.description:
Net energy gain or loss per unit physical volume for neutral particles of a
specified species and internal state, entering that population's energy
transport equation.
items.documentation:
Neutral-state power density is the net rate at which energy is transferred
to or from neutral particles of a specified species and internal state per
unit physical volume. It is the source or sink term in that population's
energy transport equation.

Its role in the state energy balance is

$$
\frac{\partial u_{s,a}}{\partial t} + \nabla\cdot\mathbf{F}_{s,a} = p_{s,a}
$$

where $s$ identifies the neutral species, $a$ identifies its internal state,
$u_{s,a}$ is that population's energy density, $t$ is time,
$\mathbf{F}_{s,a}$ is its spatial energy flux density, and $p_{s,a}$ is its
net volumetric energy source. The operator $\nabla\cdot$ denotes spatial
divergence.

The quantity combines the included energy-source and energy-sink
contributions, including applicable ionization, charge-exchange, and heating
processes. It applies to the specified internal state only, without summing
over other states or species. It is not stored energy density or a particle
production rate.

Summing over all internal states of the same neutral species gives the
[neutral power density](name:neutral_power_density), $p_s = \sum_a p_{s,a}$,
where $p_s$ is the state-summed volumetric energy source. The [ion
charge-state power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density) is the
corresponding energy-source quantity for a specified ionic charge state or
charge-state bundle rather than a neutral internal state.

Sign convention: Positive when net energy is transferred to the specified
neutral-state population.

items.name: toroidal_angular_width_of_limiter_tile
items.description:
Full toroidal angular span of one limiter tile between its minimum and
maximum φ coordinates in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal angular width of an individual limiter tile is the full angular
span occupied by that tile around the machine symmetry axis. It is a
non-negative geometric extent in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

The width is defined from the extrema of the tile's toroidal-angle extent:

$$
\Delta\phi_{\mathrm{tile}} = \phi_{\max} - \phi_{\min}
$$

where $\Delta\phi_{\mathrm{tile}}$ is the tile's toroidal angular width, and
$\phi_{\max}$ and $\phi_{\min}$ are the maximum and minimum toroidal-angle
coordinates of the tile, evaluated on a continuous angular branch when the
extent crosses the angular periodic boundary.

This quantity applies to one individual limiter tile and represents its
complete toroidal span; it is not summed over tiles, limiter units, or
periodic repetitions. It is distinct from a toroidal-angle coordinate, a
tile-center angle, and the angular width of an entire limiter assembly.

The toroidal extent complements the boundary geometry described by the
[vertical outline of the limiter
tile](name:vertical_outline_of_limiter_tile), while the analogous camera
field-of-view quantity [toroidal angular width of a
camera](name:toroidal_angular_width_of_camera) applies to an optical viewing
extent rather than a structural tile.

items.name: perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure
items.description:
Total fast-ion perpendicular pressure, summed over all fast-ion species and
charge states, is the gyrotropic stress component perpendicular to the local
magnetic field.
items.documentation:
The perpendicular total fast-ion pressure is the principal
field-perpendicular component of the gyrotropic pressure tensor of
suprathermal ions, summed over all fast-ion species and charge states. It is
one of the two independent components that characterize anisotropic fast-ion
stress relative to the local magnetic field, the other being the [parallel
total fast-ion pressure](name:parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure).

The perpendicular component is defined by the transverse second moment of
the fast-ion distribution:

$$
P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_s \sum_c \int \frac{m_s v_\perp^2}{2}\, f_{s,c}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, d^3 v
$$

where $P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the perpendicular total fast-ion pressure
at position $\mathbf{x}$, $s$ labels fast-ion species, $c$ labels charge
state, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$, $f_{s,c}$ is the fast-ion
distribution function for species $s$ and charge state $c$, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, $d^3 v$ is the velocity-space volume element, $v_\perp^2
= |\mathbf{v} - (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{b})\hat{b}|^2$ is the squared velocity
component perpendicular to the magnetic-field direction,
$\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local
magnetic field, and $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field.

This quantity applies only to the suprathermal ion population. The
aggregation convention is a direct additive sum over all fast-ion species
and over all charge states; it is not a density-weighted mean. It excludes
thermal-ion pressure, electron pressure, species-specific fast-ion pressure,
charge-state-resolved perpendicular fast-ion pressure, and the field-aligned
fast-ion component.

As a component of the [total fast-ion
pressure](name:total_fast_ion_pressure), $P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}}$ enters
the gyrotropic tensor relation
$\overleftrightarrow{P}_\mathrm{fast}=P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}}\overleftrightarrow{I}+(P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}-P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}})\hat{b}\hat{b}$,
where $\overleftrightarrow{P}_\mathrm{fast}$ is the total fast-ion pressure
tensor, $P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the [parallel total fast-ion
pressure](name:parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure), and
$\overleftrightarrow{I}$ is the identity tensor. The [perpendicular fast-ion
charge-state pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_charge_state_pressure) is
a charge-state-resolved contribution; summing the corresponding
perpendicular contributions over the included fast-ion species and charge
states gives this total component.

items.name: fast_ion_power_density
items.description:
Volumetric rate of energy transfer from coherent radio-frequency waves to
nonthermal fast ions of a selected species, summed over all ionic charge
states.
items.documentation:
Fast-ion power density is the rate at which coherent radio-frequency waves
transfer energy directly to the nonthermal fast-ion population of a selected
ion species per unit physical volume. It describes spatially resolved wave
absorption and also encompasses its flux-surface-averaged form.

The volumetric deposition rate is defined by

$$
Q_i^{\mathrm{fast}} = \frac{dP_i^{\mathrm{fast}}}{dV}
$$

where $Q_i^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-ion absorbed wave power density,
$P_i^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the wave power absorbed directly by the fast
population of ion species $i$, and $V$ is physical plasma volume.

The quantity is summed over all ionic charge states of the selected species,
not over different ion species. The [fast-ion charge-state power
density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density) resolves the
corresponding contributions by charge state or charge-state bundle. Direct
absorption by thermal ions or electrons and subsequent collisional
redistribution of the absorbed fast-ion energy are excluded.

This quantity is the fast-ion direct-wave-absorption contribution to [ion
power density](name:ion_power_density), rather than the full ion energy
source from all processes. Flux-surface averaging preserves its recipient
population and energy-transfer scope but is not required by this general
definition. The [per-toroidal-mode fast-ion power
density](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density) further resolves the
flux-surface-averaged deposition by toroidal Fourier harmonic.

items.name: deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of deuterium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally
on the last closed magnetic flux surface, summed over all ionic charge
states, and excluding neutral deuterium.
items.documentation:
Number density of deuterium ions at the plasma boundary is the local
particle count per physical volume for the deuterium-ion population
evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is
the separatrix separating magnetically confined plasma from the
open-field-line scrape-off layer.

The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is

$$
n_D(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{z>0}\int f_{D^{z+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_D$ is the deuterium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point
on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $z$ is a positive ionic charge state,
$D^{z+}$ denotes deuterium in charge state $z$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $f_{D^{z+}}$ is the velocity distribution function for that charge
state, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element.

This quantity applies specifically to deuterium ions, is evaluated locally
at the plasma boundary, and is additive over all included positive deuterium
charge states. Neutral deuterium atoms and molecules are excluded. It is
therefore distinct from the broader ion_density_at_plasma_boundary, which
does not select deuterium, and from
flux_surface_averaged_deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary, which applies a
flux-surface average rather than a local boundary evaluation.

This species-specific quantity is a specialization of
[density_at_plasma_boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), whose
particle population and charge-state aggregation are unspecified. The local
deuterium value provides the pointwise boundary quantity from which the
corresponding flux-surface-averaged deuterium density is formed.

items.name: toroidal_angle_of_beamlet_group
items.description:
Toroidal angular coordinate of a beamlet-group center around the machine
symmetry axis, using the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the toroidal angular coordinate of the representative center
position of a beamlet group about the machine symmetry axis. It locates the
group in the toroidal direction and is distinct from the position of any
individual beamlet.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the group-center
position is represented by

$$
\mathbf{r}_c = R_c\hat{\mathbf{R}}(\phi_c) + Z_c\hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_c$ is the beamlet-group center position, $R_c$ is its
major-radius coordinate, $Z_c$ is its vertical coordinate, $\phi_c$ is its
toroidal angle, $\hat{\mathbf{R}}(\phi_c)$ is the radial unit vector at that
angle, and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector. The basis is
$(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$, with $\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$.

The scope is the defined center position of the beamlet group as a whole. No
aggregation over the toroidal angles of individual beamlets is implied; the
quantity does not represent an individual beamlet's location, direction,
trajectory, radial coordinate, or vertical coordinate. Together with the
center's radial and vertical coordinates, it specifies the group's
cylindrical position. Its angular convention is the same as that used for
the [toroidal angle of an antenna
strap](name:toroidal_angle_of_antenna_strap), while the owning object is
different.

Sign convention: Positive when the center's angular displacement is in the
$+\hat{\phi}$ direction, toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: toroidal_ion_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Toroidal ion velocity at the plasma boundary is the toroidal component, in
the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the density-weighted
bulk-flow velocity of the total ion fluid at the plasma boundary. It is
distinct from random thermal motion and transport-model convection
velocities.
items.documentation:
Toroidal ion velocity at the plasma boundary is the $\hat{\phi}$ component,
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, of the density-weighted
bulk-flow velocity of the total ion fluid evaluated on the plasma-boundary
surface. It represents directed collective ion motion, not random thermal
motion.

The total-ion population aggregation is the density-weighted mean over ion
species and charge states:

$$
v_{\phi i}\big|_{\partial p} =
\frac{\sum_{\alpha,c} n_{\alpha c}\big|_{\partial p}\, v_{\phi,\alpha c}\big|_{\partial p}}
{\sum_{\alpha,c} n_{\alpha c}\big|_{\partial p}}
$$

where $v_{\phi i}\big|_{\partial p}$ is the toroidal ion velocity at the
plasma boundary, $\partial p$ denotes the plasma-boundary surface,
$n_{\alpha c}\big|_{\partial p}$ is the ion number density for species
$\alpha$ in charge state $c$ at that surface, $v_{\phi,\alpha
c}\big|_{\partial p}$ is the corresponding toroidal bulk-flow velocity
component, and the sums run over all ion species and charge states.

The scope is the total ion fluid at the plasma-boundary surface: all ion
species and all charge states contribute, with intensive velocity values
averaged by density rather than summed. It excludes electrons and neutrals,
the radial component along $\hat{R}$ or any poloidal component in the
$R$-$Z$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and the
ion velocity magnitude. A transport-model convection velocity is outside
this definition unless it is explicitly the same density-weighted toroidal
bulk-flow component at the plasma boundary.

This parent fixes toroidal projection, total-ion population aggregation, and
plasma-boundary locus, but it does not by itself prescribe an additional
averaging operation over the boundary surface. The [flux-surface-averaged
toroidal ion velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_ion_velocity_at_plasma_boundary)
is a more specific child that adds flux-surface averaging to the same
quantity rather than adding the toroidal, ion-population, or boundary
qualifiers.

Sign convention: Positive when the total-ion bulk flow at the plasma
boundary is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Total ion number density at the plasma boundary is the local particle count
per volume, summing all charged ion species and charge states while
excluding neutrals.
items.documentation:
Total ion density at the plasma boundary is the local number density of all
positively charged ion populations at the separatrix, the last closed flux
surface separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off
layer. It is the charge-state-summed specialization of ion density at the
plasma boundary.

The total ion density is defined by

$$
n_i^{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_s \sum_{Z\geq 1} n_{s,Z}
$$

where $n_{s,Z}$ is the number density of ion species $s$ in charge state
$Z$, and the sums include every charged ion species and charge state present
at the boundary.

Neutral particles are excluded, and each ion contributes one particle
regardless of its charge. The corresponding surface average is
flux-surface-averaged total ion density at the plasma boundary, which
averages this local quantity over the separatrix.

items.name: core_atomic_count_of_pellet
items.description:
Core atomic count of a pellet is the total inventory of individual atoms
contained in its core material, independent of bonding, phase, or species.
items.documentation:
Core atomic count is the inventory of individual atoms contained in the core
material of one pellet. Molecules, compounds, and mixtures are resolved into
their constituent atoms before summation, independently of bonding, phase,
and species. It is the core-restricted component of atomic count of pellet
and is distinct from the outer atomic count of pellet.

For constituent entity types indexed by $i$, the core atomic inventory is
defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{core,atom}} = \sum_i a_i N_{i,\mathrm{core}}
$$

where $N_{i,\mathrm{core}}$ is the number of core entities of type $i$ and
$a_i$ is the number of atoms in each entity. The quantity includes atoms in
the pellet core and excludes atoms in other pellet layers and separately
counted propellant gas molecules; the whole-pellet inventory is atomic count
of pellet.

items.name: toroidal_trapped_torque_density
items.description:
Toroidal trapped torque density is the local rate of change of toroidal
angular momentum per physical volume, about the symmetry axis, due to
magnetically trapped particles. It equals the major-radius lever arm times
their toroidal force density in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame.
items.documentation:
Toroidal trapped torque density is the local rate of change of toroidal
angular momentum per physical volume, about the symmetry axis, due to
magnetically trapped particles. It is defined in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The defining relation to the local toroidal force density of the trapped
population is:

$$
\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{trap}} = R f_{\phi}^{\mathrm{trap}}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi}^{\mathrm{trap}}$ is the toroidal trapped torque density,
$R$ is the major-radius lever arm measured from the symmetry axis, and
$f_{\phi}^{\mathrm{trap}}$ is the toroidal component of the trapped-particle
force density in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The trapped population consists of particles whose pitch and magnetic
mirroring cause bounce motion between turning points rather than a full
poloidal transit. This quantity excludes the passing-particle contributions
represented by
[toroidal_co_passing_torque_density](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density)
and
[toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density);
when the same distribution is partitioned by orbit class, the trapped,
co-passing, and counter-passing contributions sum to the corresponding
[toroidal_torque_density](name:toroidal_torque_density).

Sign convention: Positive when the trapped-particle toroidal force density
is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: voltage_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe
items.description:
Terminal voltage at a poloidal magnetic-field probe is the inductive voltage
at the coil terminals caused by time variation of the local poloidal
magnetic-field component in the R-Z plane of the right-handed cylindrical
(R, φ, Z) frame threading the probe windings.
items.documentation:
Terminal voltage at a poloidal magnetic-field probe is the signed
coil-terminal electromotive force associated with the probe winding that
senses the local poloidal magnetic field. The sensed field component lies in
the $R$-$Z$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame and
is projected along the probe sensitive-axis normal.

For a probe with algebraic turn count $N$ and geometric per-turn area $A$,
Faraday's law relates the terminal voltage to the local poloidal field
component $B_p$ as:

$$
V = -N A \frac{dB_p}{dt}
$$

where $V$ is the terminal voltage at the coil terminals, $B_p$ is the local
poloidal magnetic-field component along the positive sensitive-axis normal,
$N$ is the algebraic turn count including winding direction, $A$ is the
[area of poloidal magnetic-field
probe](name:area_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe), and $t$ is time.

The quantity applies to one poloidal-field probe coil and is not aggregated
over multiple probes. Its locus is specified by the major radius of poloidal
magnetic-field probe, [toroidal angle of poloidal magnetic-field
probe](name:toroidal_angle_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe), and poloidal
angle of poloidal magnetic-field probe; these position quantities identify
where the local field component is sampled and are not themselves voltages.

This quantity is distinct from the derived local poloidal magnetic field. It
is the poloidal-field-probe counterpart of [voltage of toroidal
magnetic-field probe](name:voltage_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), for a
coil oriented to sense the toroidal field, and is distinct from [voltage of
flux loop](name:voltage_of_flux_loop), which corresponds to a loop enclosing
magnetic flux rather than a local magnetic-field probe winding.

Sign convention: Positive when the poloidal magnetic flux threading the coil
in the direction of the probe's positive sensitive-axis normal is decreasing
with time.

items.name: krypton_density
items.description:
Number density of krypton ions at a point in the plasma, summed over all
ionized charge states from Kr1+ through fully stripped Kr36+ and excluding
neutral krypton atoms.
items.documentation:
Number density of krypton ions at a point in the plasma, summed over all
ionized charge states from Kr$^{1+}$ through fully stripped Kr$^{36+}$;
neutral krypton atoms are excluded.

With krypton atomic number $Z_\mathrm{Kr}=36$, the ion density is the
charge-state sum:

$$
n_\mathrm{Kr} = \sum_{q=1}^{36} n_\mathrm{Kr}^{(q)}
$$

where $n_\mathrm{Kr}^{(q)}$ is the number density of krypton ions in charge
state $q$ and the neutral state $q=0$ is omitted from the sum.

This is an extensive, charge-state-summed species density, not a
density-weighted mean over charge states and not the charge-state-resolved
[ion charge-state density](name:ion_charge_state_density), which retains the
individual $n_\mathrm{Kr}^{(q)}$ terms. It is an absolute density, distinct
from the relative [krypton
fraction](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_krypton_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density)
normalized to the electron density. The locus-specific values
[krypton_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:krypton_density_at_magnetic_axis),
krypton_density_at_pedestal, and
[krypton_density_at_divertor_target](name:krypton_density_at_divertor_target)
share this ions-only charge-state scope. In contrast,
[volume_averaged_krypton_density](name:volume_averaged_krypton_density)
includes all krypton charge states from neutral through fully stripped, so
its charge-state scope differs from this ions-only local quantity; the
[line_averaged_krypton_density](name:line_averaged_krypton_density) likewise
carries its own averaging definition.

items.name: toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Toroidal torque density transferred to bulk thermal ions through Coulomb
collisions with counter-passing fast particles.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the toroidal projection of the local angular-momentum
transfer rate per unit volume delivered to bulk thermal ions by Coulomb
collisions with counter-passing fast particles. It isolates the toroidal
component of the underlying [counter-passing thermal ion torque density due
to
collisions](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

$$
\tau_\phi^{\mathrm{cp}\to\mathrm{i}} = \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}} \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{cp}\to\mathrm{i}}
$$

Here $\tau_\phi^{\mathrm{cp}\to\mathrm{i}}$ is the toroidal torque density,
$\boldsymbol{\tau}^{\mathrm{cp}\to\mathrm{i}}$ is the corresponding
torque-density vector, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector in
the toroidal direction. The projection is defined in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Only transfer to bulk thermal ions from the counter-passing fast-particle
population is included; electron transfer and co-passing contributions are
distinct quantities.

Sign convention: Positive when the transferred angular momentum points in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: plasma_power_at_wall_due_to_recombination
items.description:
Power deposited on plasma-facing wall surfaces when incident plasma ions
recombine at the material boundary, representing the ion-channel
contribution to total wall recombination power.
items.documentation:
Plasma-ion recombination power at the wall is the rate at which
recombination energy from incident plasma ions is deposited in plasma-facing
wall material. It is the ion-channel contribution to the total wall heat
load from recombination.

The contribution is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{rec,wall}}^{\mathrm{plasma}} = \sum_s \int_A \Gamma_s^{\mathrm{ion}} E_{\mathrm{rec},s}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $s$ indexes the contributing plasma-ion species and charge states,
$\Gamma_s^{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the incident particle flux,
$E_{\mathrm{rec},s}$ is the recombination energy deposited per event, and
$A$ is the total plasma-facing wall area.

This quantity excludes surface recombination of incident neutral particles
into molecules, represented by neutral recombination power at the wall.
Together, the two channels form total recombination power at the wall, which
is distinct from volumetric [power due to
recombination](name:power_due_to_recombination).

items.name: vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Vertical neutral momentum diffusivity is the diagonal vertical component of
an effective neutral-particle momentum diffusivity tensor, governing
down-gradient redistribution of aggregate neutral momentum density along Z
in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. The vertical qualifier
identifies the flux and gradient direction, not the momentum component.
items.documentation:
Vertical neutral momentum diffusivity is the diagonal vertical component of
an effective neutral-particle momentum diffusivity tensor. It parameterizes
down-gradient diffusive transport of aggregate neutral momentum density
along the $Z$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height. The vertical qualifier identifies the flux and gradient
direction, not the momentum component.

For a diagonal Fick's-law closure, the vertical diffusive flux of a neutral
momentum-density component is

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}_{n,\alpha Z} = -D^{(n)}_{m,Z}\,\frac{\partial P_{n,\alpha}}{\partial Z}
$$

where $\alpha$ labels the transported momentum component,
$\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}_{n,\alpha Z}$ is the vertical diffusive flux of that
momentum component, $D^{(n)}_{m,Z}$ is the vertical neutral momentum
diffusivity, $P_{n,\alpha}$ is the aggregate neutral momentum density
component, and $Z$ is vertical height. The minus sign denotes down-gradient
diffusion: for positive diffusivity, the diffusive flux is directed from
larger toward smaller aggregate neutral momentum density along $Z$.

This coefficient applies to the aggregate neutral population represented by
the neutral momentum-density field. It does not denote a diffusivity for a
particular transported momentum component, and it is distinct from
off-diagonal tensor components or convective transport of neutral momentum.

items.name: accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Cumulative post-breakdown equivalent-electron inventory of neutral hydrogen
delivered by gas injection, with one count unit assigned to each hydrogen
atom.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of neutral hydrogen atoms
delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Hydrogen contributes one equivalent electron per
atom because its atomic number is one.

$$
N_{H,mathrm{gas}}(t)=Z_H\,\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_H(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{H,\mathrm{gas}}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count,
$Z_H=1$ is hydrogen's atomic number, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the
plasma-breakdown time, and $\dot{N}_H$ is the neutral-hydrogen injection
rate. The corresponding instantaneous rate is [hydrogen source rate due to
gas injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

The accumulation begins at breakdown and excludes hydrogen introduced during
prefill; it represents delivered hydrogen inventory rather than the number
of free plasma electrons or the ionization-state distribution. It is the
post-breakdown component of hydrogen count due to gas injection, distinct
from [accumulated hydrogen prefill
count](name:accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count).

items.name: line_integrated_electron_number_density
items.description:
Line-integrated electron number density is the free-electron column
abundance along the complete propagation path, including forward and return
segments when present.
items.documentation:
Line-integrated electron number density counts free electrons accumulated
along the complete electromagnetic-wave propagation path. It is the
complete-path specialization of [electron number
density](name:electron_number_density).

The defining line integral is

$$\int_0^L f\,dl$$

where $N_e$ is the free-electron column abundance, $n_e$ is the local
free-electron number density, $l$ is distance along the propagation path,
and $L$ is the total path length.

For reflected paths, forward and return segments both contribute, without a
factor-of-two correction. Electrons bound in atoms, molecules, or ions are
excluded.

This quantity is neither a local volume density nor the [line-averaged
electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density), which divides the
corresponding line integral by the length of its averaging path.

items.name: electron_temperature_at_outboard_midplane
items.description:
Kinetic temperature of the bulk electron population at the low-field-side
intersection of a chosen magnetic flux surface with the equatorial midplane.
items.documentation:
The electron temperature at the outboard midplane is the local
energy-equivalent kinetic temperature of the bulk electron population at the
low-field-side equatorial intersection of a chosen magnetic flux surface. It
is the electron-specific component of temperature at outboard midplane.

For an isotropic electron velocity distribution, the energy-equivalent
temperature is defined by

$$
T_e = \frac{2}{3}\left\langle E_{e,\mathrm{rand}} \right\rangle
$$

where $T_e$ is the electron temperature, and $\left\langle
E_{e,\mathrm{rand}} \right\rangle$ is the mean random kinetic energy per
electron, with both expressed on the same energy scale.

This quantity is local to the outboard-midplane intersection and is not a
field-line average, flux-surface average, or value at the plasma boundary.

items.name: nitrogen_source_rate
items.description:
Instantaneous rate of neutral molecular nitrogen admitted to the plasma
vessel, expressed as equivalent-electron particles with fourteen counts
assigned to each molecule.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the equivalent-electron source rate carried by neutral
molecular nitrogen admitted to the plasma vessel. It represents delivered
molecular inventory, not free-electron production, ionization rate, or
nitrogen ions retained in the plasma.

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}} = 14\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N_2}}
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron source rate and
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{N_2}}$ is the injection rate of nitrogen molecules. The
factor 14 assigns seven equivalent-electron counts to each of the two
nitrogen atoms in a molecule.

This species-resolved rate is consistent with the aggregate [source rate due
to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection). Integrating it
over a time interval gives the corresponding accumulated nitrogen inventory
represented by accumulated nitrogen count.

items.name: nuclear_target_atomic_fraction_of_neutron_detector_converter
items.description:
Dimensionless fraction of all converter atoms that are nuclei of the target
species for the primary neutron-induced detection reaction.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the normalized composition factor for target nuclei in the
converter material of a neutron detector. It identifies the share of
converter atoms belonging to the nuclear species that produces the intended
neutron-induced detection reaction.

The target atomic fraction is defined by

$$
f_{\mathrm{target}} = \frac{N_{\mathrm{target}}}{N_{\mathrm{all}}}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the number of target-species nuclei and
$N_{\mathrm{all}}$ is the total number of atoms in the converter material.
It is the nuclear-target realization of target atomic fraction of a neutron
detector converter, rather than a fraction based on converter volume, mass,
or detector efficiency. The fraction is bounded between zero and one.

items.name: radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Major-radius component of the effective velocity coefficient relating
advective, non-diffusive momentum flux to the momentum density of ions in
one specified species and charge state.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the major-radius component of the effective coefficient
describing advective, non-diffusive transport of [momentum](name:momentum)
carried by a specified ion species and charge state. It is a
transport-closure coefficient, not the bulk flow velocity of those ions.

For a selected momentum component, the convective closure is:

$$
\Pi_{s,R}^{\mathrm{conv}} = V_{s,R}^{\mathrm{mom}} g_s
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state,
$\Pi_{s,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective flux of the selected momentum
component along increasing major radius, $g_s$ is the corresponding local
momentum density, and $V_{s,R}^{\mathrm{mom}}$ is this effective convection
coefficient.

The coefficient applies to one specified ion species and charge state; it is
neither summed nor averaged over charge states. The closure term excludes
gradient-driven diffusive momentum flux, residual stress independent of
momentum density, and local momentum sources.

This quantity is the major-radius projection of the [ion charge-state
momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The major-radius
direction is not generally normal to magnetic flux surfaces. The [poloidal
ion charge-state momentum convection
velocity](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity)
resolves a different directional component of the same transport
coefficient.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective convection is directed toward
increasing major radius $R$.

items.name: fast_particle_energy
items.description:
Fast-particle energy is the total kinetic energy stored in a specified
suprathermal population, integrated over the plasma volume and including
parallel and perpendicular motion.
items.documentation:
Fast-particle energy is the global kinetic-energy content of a specified
suprathermal particle population. It includes motion both parallel and
perpendicular to the local magnetic field, without restricting the
population to ions or to a particular energization mechanism.

The defining distribution moment is:

$$
W_{\mathrm{fast}}(t)=\sum_s\int_V d^3x\int \varepsilon_s(\mathbf{p})\,f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{p},t)\,d^3p
$$

where $W_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle energy, $t$ is time, $s$
indexes the included particle species, $V$ is the plasma volume,
$\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{p}$ is particle momentum, $\varepsilon_s$
is the single-particle kinetic energy excluding rest energy, and
$f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle phase-space number density.

Only the specified fast populations contribute; the background thermal
population is excluded. Contributions from included species are summed, and
multiple fast populations of the same species are superposed without double
counting particles. This is the volume-integrated fast-population
specialization of [particle energy](name:particle_energy), not an individual
particle's energy coordinate.

The [parallel](name:parallel_fast_particle_energy) and
[perpendicular](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_energy) quantities
partition the kinetic energy according to motion along and across the local
magnetic field. In the nonrelativistic limit, their sum equals the total
fast-particle energy, with the perpendicular contribution including both
perpendicular degrees of freedom. Unlike [diamagnetic
energy](name:diamagnetic_energy), this quantity is a full fast-particle
kinetic-energy moment rather than a perpendicular-pressure-based measure
that also includes thermal populations.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless coefficient that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper
bound on particle flux for a neutral species in a specified internal state.
items.documentation:
This coefficient limits particle transport for one neutral species in one
specified internal state by setting the permitted fraction of its
collisionless free-streaming particle flux bound.

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{lim}} \le f_{\mathrm{p}}\,\Gamma_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limiting particle-flux magnitude,
$f_{\mathrm{p}}$ is this particle flux-limiter coefficient, and
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the collisionless free-streaming particle-flux
bound.

The coefficient applies to the particle channel only and to the specified
neutral internal state. No summation over neutral species or internal states
is implied, and the coefficient does not limit energy or momentum transport.
A physical limiter is nonnegative and, when used as a fraction of the
free-streaming bound, satisfies $0 \le f_{\mathrm{p}} \le 1$.

The quantity is distinct from the [neutral momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), which limits
momentum transport rather than particle transport. It also differs from the
[neutral internal-state source
rate](name:neutral_internal_state_source_rate), which represents particle
creation or destruction rather than a bound on transported particle flux.

items.name: thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface
items.description:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by the bulk thermal electron population
within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Thermal electron power at an inside flux surface quantifies the total rate
at which coherent wave energy is absorbed by the bulk thermal electron
population within the plasma volume bounded by a given magnetic flux
surface. It is the thermal-electron contribution to [electron power at an
inside flux surface](name:electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface), distinct
from the suprathermal contribution [fast electron power at an inside flux
surface](name:fast_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

The quantity is obtained by integrating the flux-surface-averaged
thermal-electron power density $p_{\mathrm{thermal,e}}$ over the enclosed
plasma volume:

$$
P_{\mathrm{thermal,e}}(\rho) = \int_0^\rho p_{\mathrm{thermal,e}}(\rho') \frac{dV}{d\rho'} \, d\rho'
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{thermal,e}}(\rho)$ is the cumulative absorbed power,
$\rho$ labels the limiting magnetic flux surface, $\rho'$ is the integration
variable, $p_{\mathrm{thermal,e}}$ is the local thermal-electron absorbed
power density, and $dV/d\rho'$ is the differential enclosed volume per unit
flux-surface label. Only absorption by bulk thermal electrons is included;
fast-electron and ion absorption, launched power, and absorption outside the
enclosed volume are excluded. At the outermost closed flux surface, it gives
the total wave power absorbed by thermal electrons.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_pressure
items.description:
Pressure of a neutral species in one internal quantum or excitation state,
equal to the isotropic part of the selected population's translational
kinetic stress.
items.documentation:
Pressure of neutral particles in one specified internal quantum or
excitation state is one-third of the trace of their translational pressure
tensor. It describes the isotropic part of that tensor without requiring an
isotropic velocity distribution.

For a selected neutral population, the defining kinetic moment is:

$$
p_{0,s,a}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{m_s}{3}\int |\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{0,s,a}(\mathbf{x})|^2 f_{0,s,a}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{0,s,a}$ is the state-resolved neutral pressure, $0$ denotes
electrical neutrality, $s$ labels the neutral species, $a$ labels its
internal state, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $m_s$ is the particle mass,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_{0,s,a}$ is the velocity distribution
of the selected population, $\mathbf{u}_{0,s,a}$ is its mean translational
velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The selected population may be thermal, suprathermal, or their combination.
The quantity retains one species and one internal state: it is neither
summed over species or internal states nor averaged over those states.
Internal excitation energy is not included in this translational moment, and
bulk-flow momentum flux is excluded by subtracting the mean velocity.

The [thermal neutral internal-state
pressure](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure) restricts this
definition to thermal particles. The [total neutral internal-state
pressure](name:total_neutral_internal_state_pressure) includes both thermal
and nonthermal particles within the same specified state; it does not denote
a sum over internal states. Contributions from a population decomposition
are additive when evaluated relative to the same mean-flow velocity.

items.name: electrostatic_potential_imaginary_part
items.description:
Electrostatic potential imaginary part is the signed quadrature component
that multiplies the imaginary unit in a complex representation of an
electrostatic potential. It denotes only that imaginary component, not the
full complex potential or its real part.
items.documentation:
Electrostatic potential imaginary part is the signed quadrature component of
an electrostatic potential represented as a complex scalar. It is the part
multiplying the imaginary unit and is defined only after a complex phase
reference has been chosen.

For a complex electrostatic potential $\Phi$, the imaginary part $\Phi_I$ is
defined by the decomposition:

$$
\Phi = \Phi_R + i\Phi_I
$$

where $\Phi_R$ is the electrostatic-potential real part, $\Phi_I$ is the
electrostatic-potential imaginary part, and $i$ is the imaginary unit.

This quantity excludes the full complex electrostatic potential and excludes
the real quadrature component. A concrete specialization is the [perturbed
electrostatic-potential imaginary
part](name:perturbed_electrostatic_potential_imaginary_part) used for a
complex perturbation representation.

Sign convention: Positive when the coefficient of $+i$ in the chosen complex
representation of the electrostatic potential is positive.

items.name: radial_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Signed major-radius component of the effective pressure-gradient transport
velocity assigned to one neutral species in a specified internal state,
distinct from direct magnetic drift of neutral particles.
items.documentation:
The radial neutral-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed
major-radius projection of an effective pressure-gradient transport velocity
assigned to one neutral species in a specified internal state in the edge
plasma. It represents a fluid-transport contribution rather than direct
magnetic drift of individual neutral particles.

For neutral species $a$ in internal state $k$, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\mathrm{dia},ak,R}=\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},ak}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $v_{\mathrm{dia},ak,R}$ is the radial velocity contribution,
$\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{dia},ak}$ is the effective diamagnetic transport
velocity assigned to that species and state, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the
unit vector toward increasing major radius. The right-handed cylindrical
frame is $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry
axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Only the specified neutral species and internal state are included; no
summation or averaging over species or states is implied. This contribution
is distinct from the state's total flow velocity. Because neutral particles
have zero net electric charge, the charged-particle diamagnetic-drift
formula does not apply directly. Radial denotes the geometric major-radius
projection, not a flux-surface-normal or magnetic-field-perpendicular
projection.

This quantity specializes [neutral-state velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) to the
cylindrical radial direction. The [vertical neutral-state velocity due to
diamagnetic
drift](name:vertical_neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift)
instead projects the same effective transport velocity onto the vertical
direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective diamagnetic transport velocity
of the specified neutral state has a component toward increasing major
radius $R$, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

items.name: neutral_power_of_divertor
items.description:
Neutral power of divertor is the total rate of neutral-particle energy
deposited on wetted plasma-facing surfaces throughout the divertor assembly.
items.documentation:
Neutral power of divertor is the total rate of neutral-particle energy
deposited on the wetted plasma-facing surfaces of the divertor assembly. It
sums neutral-particle deposition over all included divertor targets and
other divertor plasma-facing components.

The defining surface integral is

$$
P_{\mathrm{neu,div}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} q_{\mathrm{neu}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the union of the included wetted divertor
surfaces, $q_{\mathrm{neu}}$ is the neutral-particle deposited energy-flux
density on those surfaces, and $\mathrm{d}A$ is the surface-area element.
The neutral contribution includes charge-exchange neutrals and other
neutral-particle impact channels.

This quantity is the neutral-channel component of power_of_divertor. Unlike
[neutral_power_at_divertor_target](name:neutral_power_at_divertor_target),
it aggregates deposition over the divertor assembly rather than one target.
Energy carried by neutral particles that does not reach an included divertor
surface, and deposition from charged-particle, radiative, or other
non-neutral channels, is excluded.

items.name: ion_particle_source_rate
items.description:
Ion particle source rate is the net contribution of ion production and
removal to the particle-number balance of a specified ion population.
items.documentation:
Ion particle source rate is the signed contribution of ion production and
removal to an ion population's particle-number balance. This shared concept
encompasses local source terms, their explicit and density-proportional
contributions, and volume-integrated rates.

The volume-integrated form is defined by

$$
S_i(V)=\int_V s_i\,dV'
$$

where $S_i(V)$ is the net ion particle source rate integrated over the
plasma region $V$, $s_i$ is the local net volumetric [ion source
rate](name:ion_source_rate), and $dV'$ is a physical volume element. The
subscript $i$ identifies the ion population. In the cumulative form, $V$ is
the entire volume enclosed by the specified magnetic flux surface. This
integral is neither a flux-surface average nor the particle flux through
that surface.

For a specified ion species, the source is summed over all ionic charge
states without charge weighting. The [charge-state-resolved cumulative
source
rate](name:cumulative_inside_flux_surface_ion_charge_state_source_rate)
restricts the enclosed-volume integral to one charge state. The [total ion
particle source rate](name:total_ion_particle_source_rate) additionally sums
over all ion species. All contributing production and removal processes
enter the net source; positive values indicate net addition and negative
values indicate net removal. Transport across the region's boundary is a
separate particle-balance contribution.

For the local decomposition, $s_i=s_i^{\mathrm{exp}}+\alpha_i n_i$, where
$s_i^{\mathrm{exp}}$ is the additive explicit source contribution
independent of ion number density, $n_i$ is the number density of the
considered ion population, and $\alpha_i$ is the [implicit ion particle
source rate](name:implicit_ion_particle_source_rate). The implicit
coefficient must be multiplied by density to give its local
particle-production contribution; neither that coefficient nor the additive
volumetric term alone is the volume-integrated rate.

items.name: beryllium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Particle number density of beryllium ions evaluated on the flux surface
assigned to an internal transport barrier, summed over all beryllium ion
charge states and excluding neutral beryllium.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of beryllium ions evaluated on the flux surface
assigned to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the
beryllium-ion population at that flux-surface location. Beryllium has atomic
number $Z = 4$; unless a charge state is specified separately, this quantity
is the elemental beryllium ion density, summed over all beryllium ion charge
states and excluding neutral beryllium atoms. The internal transport barrier
is the designated flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field
turbulent transport can sustain steep density gradients.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Be,ITB}} = \sum_{q=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{q+},\mathrm{ITB}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be,ITB}}$ is the beryllium ion number density on the
internal-transport-barrier flux surface, $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{q+},\mathrm{ITB}}$
is the number density of beryllium charge state $q$ on the same flux
surface, and $q$ runs over positive beryllium ion charge states. The lower
limit excludes neutral beryllium.

This is an unweighted particle density, not the charge-weighted impurity
charge density or the electron density contributed by beryllium. It is a
species-specific instance of [density at the internal transport
barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier) and differs from ion
density at the internal transport barrier, which may represent a broader ion
population.

items.name: toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Toroidal component of the nitrogen impurity ion bulk-flow velocity at the
magnetic axis, taken along increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius and Z is vertical
height. It is the density-weighted mean over all nitrogen ion charge states.
items.documentation:
Toroidal component of the nitrogen impurity ion bulk-flow velocity at the
magnetic axis is the projection of the local nitrogen impurity-ion bulk flow
onto the toroidal direction at the innermost confined-plasma locus where the
poloidal magnetic-flux gradient vanishes. For this species-level intensive
quantity, the nitrogen velocity is the density-weighted mean over all
nitrogen ion charge states. The toroidal direction is $\hat{\phi}$, the unit
vector for increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases
counter-clockwise when viewed from above along $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

The charge-state-aggregated toroidal velocity is defined by the
density-weighted projection of charge-state-resolved ion flows:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{N},0}
=
\frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{N}^{q+},0}\,\left(\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{N}^{q+},0}\cdot\hat{\phi}\right)}
{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{N}^{q+},0}}
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{N},0}$ is this on-axis nitrogen toroidal velocity,
$q$ indexes nitrogen ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{N}^{q+},0}$ is the local
density of charge state $q$ at the magnetic axis,
$\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{N}^{q+},0}$ is its bulk-flow velocity at the magnetic
axis, and the subscript $0$ denotes the magnetic-axis value. The denominator
is the charge-state sum that forms [nitrogen density at the magnetic
axis](name:nitrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis).

This is a local on-axis species-level velocity, not a flux-surface-averaged
quantity and not a charge-state-summed velocity. It is defined only where
the charge-state-summed nitrogen ion density at the magnetic axis is
nonzero. It is the nitrogen counterpart, at the same locus, of [toroidal
deuterium velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis), and it is
distinguished from nitrogen toroidal velocity at other radial loci such as
[the pedestal top](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top) or [an
internal transport
barrier](name:toroidal_nitrogen_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).

Sign convention: Positive when the density-weighted nitrogen impurity-ion
flow at the magnetic axis is directed along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_iron_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of iron ions averaged over the plasma-boundary flux surface,
summed over all iron ion charge states and excluding neutral iron.
items.documentation:
Number density of iron

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Fe}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{Fe}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{Fe}}\rangle$ is the averaged iron-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the local iron-ion number density, $S$ is the
plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is the
poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude provides the averaging
weight.

This quantity applies to iron ions on the plasma-boundary flux surface and
is summed over all positive iron ion charge states, from singly ionized
through fully stripped iron. Neutral iron is excluded. The result is a
flux-surface average, not a local point value, volume average, or total iron
inventory.

It is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local [iron density at
the plasma boundary](name:iron_density_at_plasma_boundary): the same
charge-state-summed ion density is converted from a pointwise value to an
inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient-weighted surface mean. It is distinct from
[iron density at the limiter](name:iron_density_at_limiter), which refers to
a different evaluation locus.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: poloidal_electron_diffusivity
items.description:
Directional electron particle diffusion coefficient linking the poloidal
diffusive electron flux to the electron density gradient in a magnetized
plasma.
items.documentation:
Poloidal electron diffusivity is an effective scalar transport coefficient
for diffusive electron-particle transport along the poloidal direction of
flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

The constitutive relation is

$$
\Gamma_{e,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{e,\theta}\,\nabla_\theta n_e
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal component of the
diffusive electron particle-flux vector, $D_{e,\theta}$ is the poloidal
electron diffusivity, $\nabla_\theta n_e$ is the metric-scaled
electron-density gradient along increasing poloidal angle $\theta$, and
$n_e$ is electron number density. The associated flux component is positive
toward increasing $\theta$.

This is the poloidal projection of the anisotropic transport represented by
electron diffusivity. It describes diffusive transport only and excludes
convective fluxes, particle sources, and sinks; poloidal particle
diffusivity is the corresponding species-independent quantity.

items.name: neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Momentum convection velocity is an effective velocity coefficient for
advective, non-diffusive transport of momentum carried by one neutral
species, aggregated over its neutral states.
items.documentation:
Momentum convection velocity is an effective velocity coefficient for
advective, non-diffusive transport of momentum carried by a specified
neutral species. Its neutral-species form aggregates momentum over all
resolved neutral internal states and is distinct from the material bulk
velocity.

For a resolved transport direction $i$ and transported momentum component
$j$, the advective contribution to the momentum-flux tensor is defined by:

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{adv}}_{ij}=V_iP_j
$$

where $P_j$ is the selected momentum-density component,
$\Pi^{\mathrm{adv}}_{ij}$ is its advective flux, and $V_i$ is the
corresponding effective transport velocity. For a vector quantity, the
resolved $V_i$ values form the effective transport-velocity vector.

The coefficient applies only to the selected neutral species, momentum
component, and transport direction; it excludes diffusive transport,
external source terms, and the material bulk velocity. It is the
neutral-species realization of momentum convection velocity. The [toroidal
neutral-species
form](name:toroidal_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity) and
[vertical neutral-species
form](name:vertical_neutral_species_momentum_convection_velocity) show that
the component label identifies the transported momentum in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, not necessarily the direction of the
effective velocity.

items.name: incident_radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module
items.description:
The incident radiated power of a breeder blanket module is the
electromagnetic photon power from plasma radiation arriving at the module
plasma-facing surface before surface reflection losses are applied. It
includes bremsstrahlung continuum and atomic line radiation.
items.documentation:
The incident radiated power of a breeder blanket module is the
electromagnetic photon power from plasma radiation arriving at the module
plasma-facing surface before any surface reflection loss is applied. It
includes incident bremsstrahlung continuum and atomic line radiation
assigned to that module.

The incident component for a single module is defined by integrating the
incident radiative surface energy flux over the module plasma-facing
surface:

$$
P_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{inc}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{pf},m}} \Phi_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{inc}} \, dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident radiated power of the
module, $A_{\mathrm{pf},m}$ is the module plasma-facing surface, $dA$ is a
surface element, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident
photon energy flux density crossing onto that surface from the plasma side.

This quantity applies to one breeder blanket module and is the
surface-integrated total over the plasma-facing face of that module, not
over non-plasma-facing structural surfaces. It counts only incoming plasma
photon radiation and excludes reflected photon power as a separate outgoing
term. Neutron surface loads, volumetric nuclear energy deposition,
charged-particle heat fluxes, auxiliary heating, and thermal radiation
emitted by the module itself are outside this radiated-power component.

The incident component is related to the [absorbed radiated
power](name:absorbed_radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module) by the
surface-reflection balance $P_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{abs}} =
P_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{inc}} - P_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{ref}}$, equivalently
$P_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{abs}} =
(1-\mathcal{R})P_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{inc}}$ for effective reflectance
$\mathcal{R}$, where $P_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{abs}}$ is the absorbed
radiated power and $P_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reflected radiated
power. The [radiated power of a breeder blanket
module](name:radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module) identifies the module
radiation channel; it is not the arithmetic sum of incident and absorbed
components.

items.name: toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude
items.description:
Measure of how rapidly a toroidal magnetic-flux coordinate changes in space,
obtained from the magnitude of its spatial gradient.
items.documentation:
This quantity represents the local geometric rate at which a toroidal
magnetic-flux coordinate changes through physical space. It is the
magnitude-based measure derived from the spatial gradient, independent of
any particular direction or projection.

The defining relation is

$$
\left|\nabla \chi\right| = \sqrt{\nabla\chi \cdot \nabla\chi}
$$

where $\chi$ is the toroidal magnetic-flux coordinate, $\nabla$ is the
spatial-gradient operator, and the dot denotes the Euclidean inner product
of the gradient with itself.

The local form is evaluated pointwise and is not intrinsically flux-surface
averaged or squared. The [flux-surface-averaged toroidal flux coordinate
gradient
magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude)
applies a flux-surface average to this measure, while [square of toroidal
flux coordinate gradient
magnitude](name:square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude)
applies the algebraic square. Both are derived from the underlying [toroidal
flux coordinate gradient](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient), which
retains the full spatial-gradient quantity rather than its magnitude.

items.name: deuterium_density_at_limiter
items.description:
Deuterium ion number density in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to
a plasma-facing limiter surface, evaluated on the plasma side of the
magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.
items.documentation:
Deuterium density at a limiter is the local number density of deuterium ions
in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter
surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic
presheath or sheath entrance, where open scrape-off-layer field lines
terminate on the limiter material. Because deuterium carries only a single
ionization state ($\mathrm{D}^+$, charge number $Z = 1$), no charge-state
summation is required, in contrast to impurity-species counterparts such as
[carbon_density_at_limiter](name:carbon_density_at_limiter) or
[argon_density_at_limiter](name:argon_density_at_limiter).

This density, together with
[electron_temperature_at_limiter](name:electron_temperature_at_limiter),
determines the ion saturation current flux to the limiter and governs local
deuterium recycling and redeposition. In two-point model analyzes of the
scrape-off layer, the limiter-side density is linked to the upstream
separatrix density through parallel momentum and energy balance along
magnetic field lines, with the Bohm sheath criterion $v_s = c_s = \sqrt{(T_e
+ T_i)/m_i}$ setting the flow speed at the sheath entrance, where $T_e$ and
$T_i$ are the electron and ion temperatures and $m_i$ is the deuterium ion
mass.

Measurement methods include flush-mounted Langmuir probes that yield the ion
saturation current density from which the density is extracted,
spectroscopic observation of deuterium Balmer emission combined with
collisional-radiative modeling, and edge transport simulations constrained
by upstream density profiles. Representative scrape-off-layer values at the
limiter span $10^{17}$–$10^{19}$ m$^{-3}$, depending on global plasma
density, fueling, and limiter geometry.

As a member of the [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter) parent
family, this quantity complements the tritium fuel-ion counterpart
[tritium_density_at_limiter](name:tritium_density_at_limiter) and
[hydrogen_density_at_limiter](name:hydrogen_density_at_limiter). The
corresponding quantity at the magnetic separatrix is
[deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:deuterium_density_at_plasma_boundary).

items.name: parallel_neutral_energy_flux
items.description:
Parallel neutral energy flux is the net thermal energy transported per unit
area and time along the local magnetic field, summed over neutral species
and internal states.
items.documentation:
Parallel neutral energy flux is the signed thermal-energy transport carried
by neutral atoms and molecules along the local magnetic-field direction. The
reference area is perpendicular to that direction.

The field-parallel projection is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{0,W,\parallel} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,W}\cdot\frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,W,\parallel}$ is the signed parallel neutral thermal-energy
flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,W}$ is the full neutral thermal-energy flux
vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, and $|\mathbf{B}|$
is its magnitude. The projection requires a nonzero local magnetic field.

The quantity is summed over all neutral species and internal states. The
[parallel neutral internal-state energy
flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux) supplies a
state-resolved contribution to this aggregate. Energy transport carried by
ions and electrons is excluded.

This quantity specializes [neutral energy flux](name:neutral_energy_flux) by
choosing the oriented surface normal along the local magnetic field. The
field specifies the projection direction; it does not require neutral
trajectories to follow magnetic field lines.

Sign convention: Positive when neutral thermal energy is transported in the
direction of the local magnetic field.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of hydrogen ions averaged over the plasma-boundary flux
surface, with all hydrogen ion charge states summed and neutral hydrogen
excluded.
items.documentation:
Number density of hydrogen

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{H}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{H}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{H}}\rangle$ is the averaged hydrogen-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the local hydrogen-ion number density, $S$ is
the averaging flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is the
poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude is $|\nabla\psi|$.

This quantity applies to hydrogen ions on the plasma boundary, with all
hydrogen ion charge states summed and neutral hydrogen excluded. It is a
flux-surface average rather than a local point value, a volume average, or a
charge-state-resolved density.

It is the averaged counterpart of the local [hydrogen ion density at the
plasma boundary](name:hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary): the local
density is replaced by an inverse-flux-gradient-weighted surface mean. The
same averaging operation applied to another species gives a distinct
quantity, such as [flux-surface-averaged helium-4 density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary).

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector
items.description:
Vertical coordinate Z of the declared reference position of a neutral beam
injector is the signed height of that point from the equatorial plane in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical coordinate $Z$ of the declared reference position of a neutral beam
injector is the signed height of that point relative to the equatorial plane
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It identifies only the
vertical component of the injector reference-point position.

The coordinate is the projection of the reference-point displacement onto
the vertical basis vector:

$$
Z_\mathrm{NBI} = \mathbf{r}_\mathrm{ref} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_\mathrm{ref}$ is the displacement of the declared
reference position from an origin on the symmetry axis in the equatorial
plane, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

For an extended injector, this quantity locates only the declared reference
point; it does not define the injector aperture, beam-axis direction, beam
footprint, or full beam geometry. A complementary position coordinate is
[radial_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector](name:radial_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector)
when defined for the same reference point.

Sign convention: Positive when the declared reference position lies above
the equatorial plane in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction.

items.name: square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude
items.description:
Squared spatial gradient of a toroidal magnetic-flux coordinate, providing a
geometric coefficient for equilibrium descriptions in physical space.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the squared magnitude of the spatial gradient of a toroidal
magnetic-flux coordinate. It characterizes how rapidly the chosen flux
coordinate changes through physical space and serves as the geometric basis
for local and flux-surface equilibrium coefficients.

The underlying geometric measure is defined by

$$
G_\chi = \left|\nabla \chi\right|^2
$$

where $G_\chi$ is the squared flux-coordinate gradient magnitude, $\chi$ is
the toroidal magnetic-flux coordinate, $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient
operator, and the magnitude is taken with the physical-space metric.

The quantity applies to equilibrium magnetic geometry wherever the toroidal
flux coordinate and its spatial gradient are defined. Its aggregation is not
fixed at the parent level: concrete instances may be evaluated locally,
averaged over a magnetic flux surface, or formed into a ratio with another
geometric quantity.

It is distinct from the unsquared [toroidal flux-coordinate gradient
magnitude](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude), and it does
not itself prescribe a denominator such as magnetic-field strength or major
radius. The [flux-surface-averaged
square](name:flux_surface_averaged_square_of_toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude)
is the averaged instance, while related ratio quantities compare this
squared geometric factor with the squared magnetic-field magnitude or
squared major radius.

items.name: reflected_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
items.description:
Reflected power of a lower-hybrid antenna module is the RF power returning
toward the source through the transmission line because of impedance
mismatch at the plasma–antenna interface.
items.documentation:
Reflected power of a lower-hybrid antenna module is the nonnegative RF power
propagating back toward the source because of impedance mismatch at the
plasma–antenna interface. It is the returning-power component of the
wave-power budget represented by [power of a lower-hybrid
antenna](name:power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna), evaluated at the module input
reference plane.

The module power components satisfy:

$$
P_\mathrm{launched} = P_\mathrm{forward} - P_\mathrm{reflected}
$$

where $P_\mathrm{forward}$ is the [forward
power](name:forward_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) arriving at the module
