input reference plane, $P_\mathrm{reflected}$ is the reflected power
returning toward the source, and $P_\mathrm{launched}$ is the net [launched
power](name:launched_power_of_lower_hybrid_antenna) entering the vacuum
vessel from that module. All three components refer to the same module and
reference plane.

Reflected power is the portion of forward power returned toward the source,
distinct from net launched power and power absorbed by the plasma. The
quantity applies to one antenna module and is not a sum over modules or
antennas.

items.name: ion_average_temperature_at_limiter
items.description:
Density-weighted mean kinetic temperature of all ion species and charge
states on the plasma-facing side of a limiter, providing the ion component
of the local average plasma temperature.
items.documentation:
The ion component of the local plasma temperature at a limiter is the
density-weighted mean kinetic temperature of all positive ion species and
charge states on the plasma-facing side of the limiter. It is the
ion-specific component of average temperature at the limiter.

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{avg}} = \frac{\sum_s \sum_q n_{s,q} T_{s,q}}{\sum_s \sum_q n_{s,q}}
$$

where $s$ indexes ion species, $q$ indexes their positive charge states,
$n_{s,q}$ is the corresponding ion number density, and $T_{s,q}$ is its
kinetic temperature. The denominator is the [total ion density at the
limiter](name:total_ion_density_at_limiter).

This quantity includes all ion species and charge states in the local plasma
population and excludes electrons, neutral particles, and the solid limiter
material. It is distinct from temperature at the limiter, which may denote a
specified population or a different population aggregation.

items.name: alpha_angle_of_passive_loop_element
items.description:
Signed inclination of the first axis of an oblique passive conductor
loop-element cross-section, measured counterclockwise from the outward
radial direction in the poloidal plane.
items.documentation:
The alpha angle is the signed inclination of the first axis of an oblique,
trapezoidal or parallelogram-shaped cross-section of one passive conductor
loop element. It specifies the orientation of that element’s cross-sectional
geometry in the poloidal plane.

The angle is defined from the directed first-axis vector:

$$
\alpha = \operatorname{atan2}\!\left(\mathbf{a}_1 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{Z}},\,\mathbf{a}_1 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}\right)
$$

where $\alpha$ is the alpha inclination angle, $\mathbf{a}_1$ is the
directed first axis of the cross-section, $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the outward
radial unit vector, $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the upward vertical unit vector,
and $\operatorname{atan2}$ returns the signed angle from the radial
component to the vertical component. These directions are defined in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies independently to each passive loop element and to its
own oblique cross-section; it is not an aggregate angle for a complete
passive loop or a collection of elements. It describes the first
cross-sectional axis only, not the transverse dimensions of the element and
not the overall loop reference-axis inclination represented by the [tilt
angle of the passive loop](name:tilt_angle_of_passive_loop). The alpha angle
supplies orientation information for interpreting the element’s other
cross-sectional geometry, but does not determine those dimensions.

Sign convention: Positive when the first axis rotates counterclockwise from
the outward radial direction toward the positive vertical direction in the
poloidal plane.

items.name: normalized_debye_length
items.description:
Dimensionless ratio of the multispecies Debye shielding length to the
positive reference length used by the gyrokinetic formulation.
items.documentation:
The multispecies Debye shielding length is the electrostatic screening scale
produced by the combined response of all charged species. This quantity
expresses that scale relative to the positive reference length selected for
the gyrokinetic formulation.

$$
\lambda_{D,\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{1}{L_{\mathrm{ref}}}\left(\sum_s \frac{n_s q_s^2}{\epsilon_0 k_B T_s}\right)^{-1/2}
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density of species $s$, $q_s$ is its particle
charge, $T_s$ is its thermodynamic temperature, $k_B$ is Boltzmann's
constant, $\epsilon_0$ is the vacuum permittivity, and $L_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is
the gyrokinetic reference length. The sum includes the charged species
contributing to quasistatic Debye shielding and excludes neutral
populations. The underlying shielding length also enters the [Coulomb
logarithm](name:coulomb_logarithm); this normalized quantity is not a
species-specific screening length.

items.name: effective_spectral_width_of_spectrometer_channel
items.description:
Response-equivalent wavelength interval of a spectrometer channel, defined
from the full spectral instrument function rather than a Gaussian
approximation.
items.documentation:
Effective spectral width is the wavelength interval equivalent to the area
of the spectrometer channel's normalized instrument-function response. It
captures the integrated response of non-Gaussian line shapes and is distinct
from the Gaussian standard-deviation measure named by spectral width of a
spectrometer channel.

$$
W_{\mathrm{eff}} = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{R(\lambda)}{R_{\max}}\,d\lambda
$$

where $R(\lambda)$ is the channel response to monochromatic radiation at
wavelength $\lambda$, and $R_{\max}$ is its peak response. For a Gaussian
response with standard deviation $\sigma$, the equivalent width is
$W_{\mathrm{eff}} = \sqrt{2\pi}\,\sigma$; therefore, this quantity is not
numerically identical to the Gaussian spectral width.

items.name: toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Toroidal krypton velocity at the pedestal top is the toroidal component of
the density-weighted mean krypton ion bulk-flow velocity at the H-mode
pedestal top, taken over all krypton charge states. It is resolved along
increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame,
where R is major radius and Z is vertical height.
items.documentation:
Toroidal krypton velocity at the pedestal top is the toroidal component of
the krypton ion bulk-flow velocity evaluated at the H-mode pedestal-top
reference location. As a species-level intensive quantity, it is the
density-weighted mean over all krypton ion charge states, not a sum of
charge-state velocities. The toroidal direction is the $\hat{\phi}$ basis
direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The charge-state aggregation and toroidal projection are defined by

$$
v_{\phi}^{\mathrm{Kr}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}\left(\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}} \cdot \hat{\phi}\right)}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes krypton ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$ is the
number density of charge state $q$ in m$^{-3}$,
$\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{Kr}^{q+}}$ is its bulk-flow velocity, and
$v_{\phi}^{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the resulting signed species-level toroidal
velocity.

This quantity is inferred from krypton line spectroscopy or other
impurity-flow diagnostics localized near the pedestal top, with
viewing-geometry corrections used to isolate the toroidal component. Because
line emission is often charge-state selective, interpretation must map
measured charge-state velocities onto the density-weighted species mean.
Momentum-balance or radial-force-balance analysis may combine this quantity
with poloidal krypton velocity at the pedestal top, pressure-gradient,
electric-field, and magnetic-field information.

No universal krypton-specific pedestal range applies across devices.
Representative signed impurity toroidal velocities at pedestal-top
conditions are commonly in the range $-5 \times 10^4$ to $5 \times 10^4$
m.s$^{-1}$, with higher-rotation cases approaching $\pm 10^5$ m.s$^{-1}$ in
either toroidal direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the density-weighted krypton ion bulk flow at
the pedestal top is along $+\hat{\phi}$, the direction of increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: upper_wavelength_of_filter
items.description:
Upper wavelength of a filter specifies the long-wavelength,
low-photon-energy boundary of its transmitted passband as a vacuum spectral
coordinate.
items.documentation:
Wavelength of filter

The upper wavelength bound corresponds to the lower frequency boundary of
the same passband:

$$
\lambda_{\mathrm{u}} = \frac{c}{\nu_{\min}}
$$

where $\lambda_{\mathrm{u}}$ is the upper wavelength bound, $c$ is the speed
of light in vacuum, and $\nu_{\min}$ is the lower frequency boundary of the
passband.

This quantity is the upper-edge specialization of [wavelength of a
filter](name:wavelength_of_filter), not its nominal band center or
bandwidth. Together with the [lower wavelength
bound](name:lower_wavelength_of_filter), it delimits the specified
transmission interval; the difference between these bounds is the wavelength
span. It denotes a vacuum spectral coordinate, not the wavelength inside the
filter material.

items.name: right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_imaginary_part
items.description:
Signed imaginary quadrature of the right-hand circular E-minus wave
electric-field phasor along a beam or ray path, relative to a specified
phase reference.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the imaginary quadrature of the right-hand circularly
polarized E-minus component of a wave [electric field](name:electric_field)
phasor along its propagation path. It retains signed phase information and
is not the field amplitude or the instantaneous physical electric field.

The defining relation is:

$$
E_{-,I} = \operatorname{Im}(E_-)
$$

where $E_{-,I}$ is the signed imaginary quadrature, $E_-$ is the [right-hand
circularly polarized wave electric-field
phasor](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field), and
$\operatorname{Im}$ selects its imaginary part.

The parent polarization component is transverse to the local static magnetic
field. This quadrature is evaluated locally along the beam or ray
propagation path, including electron cyclotron emission paths; it is not
integrated along that path. It inherits the circular-polarization basis and
phase reference of the parent phasor.

Together with the [right-hand circularly polarized real
part](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_real_part),
it reconstructs the parent component through $E_- = E_{-,R} + iE_{-,I}$,
where $E_{-,R}$ is the real, in-phase quadrature and $i$ is the imaginary
unit. Changing the phase reference mixes the two quadratures without
changing the physical polarization.

Sign convention: Positive when the E-minus phasor lies in the upper half of
the complex plane defined by the specified phase reference.

items.name: thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_thermalization
items.description:
Angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume deposited in thermal ions
when fast particles undergo thermalization.
items.documentation:
This torque-density vector is the angular-momentum source deposited in the
thermal-ion population by the thermalization of fast particles. It
represents only the momentum transfer associated with this process, rather
than the total torque acting on the ions.

The torque-density vector is defined from the thermal-ion angular-momentum
density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{th}} = \left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}_{\mathrm{th}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{thermalization}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the torque-density vector,
$\boldsymbol{\ell}_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the angular-momentum density of the
thermal-ion population, and $t$ is time.

Only transfer caused by fast-particle thermalization is included;
contributions from other momentum-transfer processes are excluded. The
toroidal projection is represented by the [toroidal thermal-ion torque
density due to
thermalization](name:toroidal_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_thermalization).

Sign convention: Positive when a component of the torque points along the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ basis.

items.name: linear_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux
items.description:
Linear neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the vector-valued
signed transport rate of linear momentum carried by neutral particles in one
specified internal state across an oriented surface.
items.documentation:
The linear neutral internal-state momentum flux density is the vector-valued
transport of linear momentum carried by neutral particles restricted to one
specified atomic, molecular, charge, or excitation state. It describes
momentum transport rather than particle-number transport or a local momentum
source.

For an oriented surface, the momentum-flux vector is defined by

$$
\mathbf{F}_{\Pi}^{(s)}(\hat{n}) = \boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)} \cdot \hat{n} = \int m_s\mathbf{v}\, (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{n}) f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $s$ identifies the internal state, $\hat{n}$ is the oriented surface
normal, $m_s$ is the particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$
is the state-resolved velocity distribution, and $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{(s)}$ is
the corresponding momentum-flux tensor.

This is the linear-momentum form of the parent neutral internal-state
momentum flux. Projection onto a specified direction produces components
such as [poloidal linear neutral internal-state momentum
flux](name:poloidal_linear_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux); no
particular radial, poloidal, toroidal, vertical, or magnetic-field-parallel
direction is implied here.

Sign convention: Positive when particles cross the oriented surface in its
positive normal direction while carrying linear momentum in the selected
positive direction.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_particle_flux
items.description:
Poloidal neutral particle flux is the net particle crossing rate per unit
area normal to the poloidal direction for one neutral species, summed over
internal states.
items.documentation:
Poloidal neutral particle flux is the local signed number flow of one
neutral atomic or molecular species around the magnetic axis, divided by the
actual area perpendicular to the local poloidal direction. Crossings in
opposite directions contribute with opposite signs.

The poloidal projection is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{p}} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal neutral particle flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0$ is the neutral particle number-flux vector summed
over internal states, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the local unit
vector in the positive poloidal direction. This direction lies in a
constant-$\phi$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity applies to one neutral species and sums over all its internal
states, rather than selecting the state represented by [poloidal neutral
internal-state particle
flux](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux). The
state-resolved contributions sum to this quantity. It is a local net flux
per unit area, not an area-integrated arrival rate or an incident-only flux.

This quantity specializes [neutral particle
flux](name:neutral_particle_flux) to an oriented surface whose normal is the
local poloidal direction. The poloidal direction is geometric and must not
be identified with the magnetic-field direction used for [parallel neutral
particle flux](name:parallel_neutral_particle_flux).

Sign convention: Positive when neutral particles travel clockwise around the
magnetic axis in a poloidal plane viewed with the toroidal symmetry axis to
the left and increasing $Z$ upward.

items.name: derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_poloidal_magnetic_flux_coordinate
items.description:
Geometric rate of change of the cumulative volume enclosed by a nested
magnetic flux surface as its signed poloidal flux coordinate varies.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the geometric derivative of the cumulative volume enclosed
by a nested magnetic flux surface with respect to its signed poloidal
magnetic-flux coordinate.

It is defined by

$$
\frac{dV}{d\psi}=\frac{d}{d\psi}V(\psi)
$$

where $V(\psi)$ is the volume enclosed by the flux surface labeled by
$\psi$, $\psi$ is the signed poloidal magnetic-flux coordinate, and
$d/d\psi$ denotes differentiation with respect to that coordinate.

The quantity applies separately to each nested closed flux surface. The
underlying volume is cumulative from the magnetic axis to the selected
surface, so this derivative describes the change in enclosed volume along
the flux coordinate rather than a local volume density, a shell volume, or a
plasma-population-weighted quantity.

It is the derivative of [volume enclosed by a flux
surface](name:volume_of_flux_surface); integrating it between two
flux-coordinate values gives the difference between the corresponding
enclosed volumes. It is distinct from the derivative with respect to the
toroidal flux coordinate, which is represented by [derivative of volume with
respect to toroidal flux
coordinate](name:derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate).

Sign convention: Positive when the enclosed volume increases in the
direction of increasing signed poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$.

items.name: brightness_of_visible_camera
items.description:
Visible-camera brightness is band-integrated photon radiance along a
specified viewing direction over the wavelengths admitted by a visible
passband. It gives the photon rate per projected collecting area and
accepted solid angle, with the spectral dependence integrated over that
band.
items.documentation:
Visible-camera brightness is the photon radiance of a radiation field along
a specified viewing direction after integration over a visible wavelength
interval or passband. It is normalized to projected collecting area,
observation time, and accepted solid angle, and counts photons rather than
radiant energy.

The band-integrated photon radiance is defined by integrating the spectral
photon radiance over the visible passband:

$$
B_\mathrm{vis} = \int_{\lambda_1}^{\lambda_2} L_\lambda^{(\gamma)}(\lambda)\, d\lambda
$$

where $B_\mathrm{vis}$ is the visible-camera brightness,
$L_\lambda^{(\gamma)}(\lambda)$ is the spectral photon radiance at
wavelength $\lambda$, and $[\lambda_1,\lambda_2]$ is the wavelength interval
defining the visible passband.

The quantity is non-negative because spectral photon radiance is
non-negative over the passband. It is distinct from spectral radiance, which
retains wavelength dependence, and from [radiance at spectral
line](name:photon_radiance_at_spectral_line), which refers to an individual
spectral line or narrow line interval; it also differs from energy radiance
because photons are counted without weighting by photon energy.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description:
Ratio of volume-averaged tritium density to volume-averaged electron density
is the volume-averaged tritium number density, summed over all charge
states, divided by the volume-averaged electron number density.
items.documentation:
Ratio of volume-averaged tritium density to volume-averaged electron density
is the volume-averaged tritium number density divided by the volume-averaged
electron number density. It expresses the tritium contribution to plasma
composition relative to the electron population after both densities have
been averaged over the same plasma volume.

The ratio is defined as:

$$
f_{T/e}^{V} = \frac{\langle n_T \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $f_{T/e}^{V}$ is this ratio, $\langle n_T \rangle_V$ is the
[volume-averaged tritium density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density),
$\langle n_e \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), $n_T$ is the local [tritium
density](name:tritium_density), $n_e$ is the local [electron
density](name:electron_density), and $\langle q\rangle_V$ denotes
$V^{-1}\int_V q\,dV$ for scalar field $q$ over the common plasma volume $V$.

The scope is the specified plasma volume and the particle populations
contained in that volume. The tritium density is a species-level per-volume
amount and is therefore summed over all tritium charge states before volume
averaging. The definition contains no selection by the time of peak electron
density or by any other operating condition.

This quantity is the ratio of volume averages, not the volume average of the
local ratio $n_T/n_e$, and it is not normalized to the total hydrogenic-fuel
density. It is the tritium-only counterpart of the [ratio of volume-averaged
deuterium-tritium density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
which uses the combined deuterium-plus-tritium numerator; it also differs
from the local ratio of tritium density to electron density.

items.name: radial_ion_momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Diffusion coefficient relating the diffusive radial ion momentum flux to the
local radial ion momentum gradient, expressing down-gradient redistribution
within the total ion population summed over charge states.
items.documentation:
The radial ion momentum diffusivity $D_{[3m\mathrm{rad}}^i$ is the effective
diffusion coefficient characterizing down-gradient redistribution of the
radial component of momentum across magnetic flux surfaces within the total
ion population summed over all charge states. It is the radial component of
the broader ion momentum diffusivity.

The flux-surface-integrated diffusive radial ion momentum flux is
represented by

$$
\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{mom},i,r}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -V'\mathcal{M}_iD_{\mathrm{rad}}^i\left\langle \left|\nabla\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}\right|^2 \right\rangle \frac{d v_{r,i}}{d\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}}
$$

where $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{mom},i,r}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux
of radial ion momentum through a flux surface, $V'$ is the derivative of
enclosed volume with respect to the normalized toroidal-flux coordinate
$\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$, $\mathcal{M}_i$ is the total ion mass density,
$v_{r,i}$ is the radial component of the mean ion fluid velocity, $\nabla$
is the spatial gradient, and angle brackets denote a flux-surface average.

The coefficient applies to the total ion population, with contributions
summed over ion species and all charge states. Here radial denotes the
flux-surface transport direction associated with increasing
$\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$, not a cylindrical-$R$ projection; parallel and
poloidal momentum channels are distinct quantities. Unlike [ion-state
momentum diffusivity](name:ion_state_momentum_diffusivity), this quantity is
not resolved by charge state.

Replacing the radial momentum component with the poloidal component gives
the corresponding [poloidal ion momentum
diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusivity); both are directional
components of ion momentum diffusivity, while the minus sign expresses
down-gradient diffusive transport.

items.name: maximum_force_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description:
Upper allowable value of a signed electromagnetic force resultant for a
poloidal-field coil, with magnitude and sign defined by one
force-combination-matrix row.
items.documentation:
Maximum force of a poloidal-field coil is the upper allowable value of a
signed electromagnetic force resultant acting on the coil. It bounds the
resultant derived from radial and vertical Lorentz-force components and is
distinct from the actual [force of a poloidal-field
coil](name:force_of_poloidal_field_coil).

For matrix row $m$, the associated force resultant is defined by

$$
F_m = a_m F_R + b_m F_Z
$$

where $F_R$ is the [radial force of a poloidal-field
coil](name:radial_force_of_poloidal_field_coil), $F_Z$ is the [vertical
force of a poloidal-field coil](name:vertical_force_of_poloidal_field_coil),
and $a_m$ and $b_m$ are the row-specific force-combination weights. The
maximum-force quantity is the upper allowable value assigned to the selected
resultant; it is not a separate Lorentz-force component.

Sign convention: Positive when the weighted combination of outward radial
force and upward vertical force, resolved in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, is positive.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Fick's-law neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient multiplying
the temperature gradient of neutral particles in one internal state in
diffusive thermal-energy transport, serving as the direction-agnostic parent
over its radial and poloidal component forms.
items.documentation:
Fick's-law neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient is the scalar
diffusivity that relates Fickian diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by
neutral particles in a specified internal state to the temperature gradient
of those same particles. It is resolved for one internal state, not summed
or averaged over internal states, and is independent of any chosen spatial
projection.

The isotropic Fickian contribution is defined by

$$
\mathbf{q}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s} = - n_{n,s} D_{E,n,s} \nabla T_{n,s}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy
flux carried by neutral particles in internal state $s$, $n_{n,s}$ is their
number density, $D_{E,n,s}$ is this coefficient, and $T_{n,s}$ is their
temperature.

The coefficient includes only the Fickian term driven by $\nabla T_{n,s}$
and excludes convective energy transport, sources, sinks, and effective
coefficients that absorb non-diffusive contributions. It specializes the
internal-state energy diffusion coefficient to neutral particles and is the
internal-state-resolved counterpart of the [neutral energy diffusion
coefficient](name:neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

As the direction-agnostic parent, it is distinct from the [radial neutral
internal-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient),
where radial denotes the $\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and from the [poloidal neutral internal-state energy
diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

items.name: requested_voltage_of_neutron_detector
items.description:
Voltage of a neutron detector specified as the high-voltage supply setpoint
that establishes the target detector bias, rather than the actual output
voltage.
items.documentation:
Voltage of neutron detector

The requested bias is defined by:

$$
U = \varphi_{\mathrm{bias}}^{\mathrm{req}} - \varphi_{\mathrm{ref}}
$$

where $U$ is the requested bias voltage,
$\varphi_{\mathrm{bias}}^{\mathrm{req}}$ is the commanded potential of the
biased detector terminal, and $\varphi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the supply
reference-terminal potential.

This setpoint is distinct from the actual supply output voltage and from the
low-voltage supply setting for detector electronics. The [requested voltage
of a spectrometer channel](name:requested_voltage_of_spectrometer_channel)
has the corresponding high-voltage bias-setpoint role for that channel.

Sign convention: Positive when the commanded detector-bias potential exceeds
the supply reference-terminal potential.

items.name: toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part
items.description:
Toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic-field real part is the in-phase φ
component, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of the complex
first-order plasma magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction for one
specified toroidal Fourier harmonic. In this frame, R is major radius, φ is
toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height.
items.documentation:
Toroidal perturbed plasma magnetic-field real part is the real component of
the toroidal projection of the complex first-order plasma magnetic-field
perturbation eigenfunction in the plasma region for one specified toroidal
Fourier harmonic. The toroidal projection is the component along
$\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$
is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when
viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The physical toroidal perturbation associated with the complex eigenfunction
is represented by

$$
\delta B_\phi(R,\phi,Z,t) = \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\delta\tilde{B}_\phi(R,Z)\exp\!\left(i(n\phi-\omega t)\right)\right]
$$

where $\delta B_\phi$ is the physical first-order toroidal magnetic-field
perturbation, $\delta\tilde{B}_\phi$ is the complex toroidal eigenfunction
amplitude, $\operatorname{Re}$ denotes the real-part operator, $n$ is the
toroidal mode number, $\omega$ is the mode angular frequency, and $t$ is
time. This quantity is $\operatorname{Re}[\delta\tilde{B}_\phi(R,Z)]$.

Together with
[toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part),
this quantity specifies the complex toroidal perturbation component
[toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field)
for the selected harmonic. It is distinct from the radial and poloidal
real-part components
[radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part)
and
[poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part),
from the equilibrium toroidal magnetic field, and from the vacuum-region
counterpart
[toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part).
A global complex phase rotation of the eigenfunction changes the split
between real and imaginary parts while leaving the reconstructed physical
perturbation unchanged when the same Fourier convention is used.

Sign convention: Positive when $\operatorname{Re}[\delta\tilde{B}_\phi]$ is
directed along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: trapped_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Collisional torque density for trapped fast ions is the local vector rate of
angular-momentum transfer per unit volume caused by Coulomb collisions with
background plasma species.
items.documentation:
Collisional torque density for trapped fast ions is the local source density
of angular momentum transferred to or from the trapped fast-ion population
by Coulomb collisions. It retains the full torque-density vector rather than
selecting a single directional component.

The torque-density vector is defined from the collisional force density as

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{fast,trapped}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{fast,trapped}}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the torque reference
origin and $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{\mathrm{fast,trapped}}$ is the
collisional force density transferred to the trapped fast-ion population.
Its components are represented in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

The quantity is restricted to trapped fast-ion orbits and excludes torque
from noncollisional mechanisms. The unrestricted [fast-ion torque density
due to collisions](name:fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions) provides
the broader parent quantity, while [toroidal trapped fast-ion torque density
due to
collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
is its toroidal component. The related [toroidal fast-ion torque density due
to collisions](name:toroidal_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
selects the toroidal component without the trapped-orbit restriction.

Sign convention: Positive when the relevant torque-density component points
along the corresponding positive basis vector of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: power_density_due_to_radiation
items.description:
Local volumetric rate at which plasma energy is converted into emitted
electromagnetic radiation, with positive values denoting energy loss from
the plasma.
items.documentation:
Radiative power density is the local rate of electromagnetic energy emission
per unit volume, summed over the radiation mechanisms included by the
physical model. It describes energy leaving the plasma as radiation rather
than energy transferred through collisional, conductive, or convective
channels.

$$
p_{\mathrm{rad}} = \frac{\partial E_{\mathrm{rad}}}{\partial V\,\partial t}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is the radiative power density, $E_{\mathrm{rad}}$
is emitted electromagnetic energy, $V$ is plasma volume, and $t$ is time. As
a radiative specialization of power_density, it may include line radiation,
continuum radiation, and other modeled emission processes; it excludes
energy that remains in the plasma or is transferred by nonradiative
channels.

Sign convention: Positive when energy leaves the plasma as emitted
electromagnetic radiation.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_ece_channel
items.description:
Signed vertical coordinate of an electron-cyclotron-emission channel’s
measurement position in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The vertical coordinate of an electron-cyclotron-emission (ECE) channel is
the signed projection of its measurement position onto the vertical
direction.

$$
Z_{\mathrm{ECE}} = \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{ECE}} \cdot \hat{Z}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{ECE}}$ is the vertical coordinate,
$\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{ECE}}$ is the position vector of the channel’s
measurement location, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity applies to the measurement position associated with one ECE
channel and is not averaged or summed over channels. It describes the
channel position rather than an ECE signal, frequency, or plasma-field
value.

It is distinct from the radial coordinate $R$ and toroidal angle $\phi$. The
[vertical coordinate of a measurement
position](name:vertical_coordinate_of_measurement_position) expresses the
same geometric quantity for a generic measurement location, whereas this
entry retains the ECE-channel locus.

Sign convention: Positive when the ECE channel measurement position lies in
the direction of increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
items.description:
Vertical coordinate of the geometric center of an electron-cyclotron
launcher mirror in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical coordinate of the geometric center of an electron-cyclotron
launcher mirror is the $Z$ coordinate of that center in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The coordinate is defined by projecting the mirror geometric-center position
onto the vertical coordinate axis:

$$
z_m = Z(\mathbf{r}_{m,c})
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_{m,c}$ is the position of the electron-cyclotron launcher
mirror geometric center and $Z(\mathbf{r}_{m,c})$ is its vertical
coordinate.

Together with the radial centroid of the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror
and the [toroidal coordinate of the electron-cyclotron launcher
mirror](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror),
this quantity specifies the mirror geometric-center position in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is distinct from
coordinates defined for other mirror reference points, such as a sphere
center or a surface point.

items.name: toroidal_counter_passing_current_density
items.description:
Toroidal current density driven locally by counter-passing particles,
including direct charge transport and the collisional back-current carried
by electrons and thermal ions.
items.documentation:
Toroidal current density attributed to counter-passing particles is the
local, signed toroidal projection of the net current driven by that orbit
class. It includes direct particle charge transport and the associated
collisional back-current carried by electrons and thermal ions.

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\phi,\mathrm{cp}} = \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}\cdot\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{cp}}
$$

where $j_{\phi,\mathrm{cp}}$ is the toroidal counter-passing current
density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the [counter-passing current-density
vector](name:counter_passing_current_density), and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$
is the toroidal unit vector. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, $R$ is the distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ points toward
increasing $\phi$.

Counter-passing particles occupy untrapped passing orbits circulating
opposite to the plasma-current direction. This quantity is evaluated locally
at a position in a poloidal cross-section, not averaged over a magnetic flux
surface. Its aggregation includes the direct current and the back-current
attributed to this population, rather than all contributions to plasma
[current density](name:current_density).

Unlike [toroidal counter-passing fast current
density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_current_density), which excludes
compensating return currents, this quantity retains the associated electron
and thermal-ion back-current. It is a signed component of the parent vector,
not its magnitude or its magnetic-field-parallel projection.

Sign convention: Positive when the net conventional current attributed to
counter-passing particles flows toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$,
counter-clockwise when viewed from above.

items.name: radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Signed major-radius projection of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic
fluid velocity for one ion charge state, distinct from individual
guiding-center motion and total radial flow.
items.documentation:
The radial ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed
major-radius projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid drift for one
ion charge state. It represents a local fluid-moment contribution rather
than the guiding-center motion of individual ions and is not restricted to
the plasma edge.

For a magnetized ion charge state labeled $\alpha$ with scalar partial
pressure, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\ast\alpha,R} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $v_{\ast\alpha,R}$ is the radial diamagnetic-drift velocity component,
$p_\alpha$ is the charge state's partial pressure, $\nabla p_\alpha$ is its
pressure gradient, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector,
$B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $q_\alpha$ is the signed particle charge,
and $n_\alpha$ is the charge-state number density. The unit vector
$\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ points toward increasing major radius in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal
symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Only the specified ion species and charge state are included; no averaging
over charge states or species is implied. This contribution excludes
electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent
parallel flow; it is not the total radial velocity. Cylindrical radial
projection is distinct from flux-surface-normal projection and does not by
itself represent transport across magnetic flux surfaces. Although the
diamagnetic drift vector is perpendicular to the magnetic field, its
cylindrical radial component need not vanish.

For a species-level velocity, the diamagnetic contribution is the
density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states, not their sum. The
[binormal ion velocity due to diamagnetic
drift](name:binormal_ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is the binormal
projection of that species-level mean, rather than the charge-state-resolved
cylindrical radial projection defined here.

Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic fluid velocity has a
component toward increasing major radius $R$, away from the toroidal
symmetry axis.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_argon_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of argon ions averaged over the last closed magnetic flux
surface, summed over all argon ion charge states and excluding neutral
argon.
items.documentation:
Number density of argon

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle = \oint n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{\mathrm{Ar}}\rangle$ is the averaged argon-ion number
density, $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the local argon-ion number density, $S$ is the
plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface element, and $\psi$ is the
poloidal magnetic flux; $|\nabla\psi|$ is the magnitude of its spatial
gradient.

This quantity is summed over all charged argon ion states and excludes
neutral argon. It is a flux-surface average rather than a local point value,
line average, or volume average.

It is the averaged counterpart of the local [argon ion
density](name:argon_density) and differs from the [volume-averaged argon
density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density), which uses a plasma-volume
average instead of an inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient-weighted surface
average. Its species-specific structure parallels the [flux-surface-averaged
xenon density at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_xenon_density_at_plasma_boundary).

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: ethylene_prefill_count
items.description:
Ethylene prefill count is the total amount of neutral ethylene (C2H4)
introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron
count with 16 equivalent electrons per molecule.
items.documentation:
Ethylene prefill count is the total amount of neutral ethylene (C2H4)
introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Each neutral ethylene molecule contributes
sixteen equivalent electrons: twelve from two carbon atoms and four from
four hydrogen atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_2H_4,prefill}} = (2Z_{\mathrm{C}}+4Z_{\mathrm{H}})N_{\mathrm{C_2H_4,prefill}} = 16N_{\mathrm{C_2H_4,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}16\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_4}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{C}}=6$ and $Z_{\mathrm{H}}=1$ are the atomic numbers of
carbon and hydrogen, $N_{\mathrm{C_2H_4,prefill}}$ is the accumulated
ethylene-molecule count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_4}}$ is the ethylene
introduction rate, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and
plasma-breakdown times.

This quantity includes only neutral ethylene introduced before breakdown and
excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas
injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the ethylene component
of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count);
[accumulated_ethylene_count](name:accumulated_ethylene_count) represents the
distinct post-breakdown accumulation, while
[ethane_prefill_count](name:ethane_prefill_count) applies the same
convention to a different molecule.

items.name: neutral_state_particle_diffusivity
items.description:
Effective Fickian transport coefficient relating neutral-state particle flux
to neutral-state number-density gradients, with directional components
represented by more specific quantities.
items.documentation:
Neutral-state particle diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient
for particle spreading driven by a neutral-state number-density gradient. It
is the neutral-charge-state specialization of [particle
diffusivity](name:particle_diffusivity), with directional components
represented by more specific quantities.

For each resolved direction $i$, the diffusive particle flux of neutral
state $\alpha$ is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\alpha,i}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\alpha,i}\,\frac{\partial n_\alpha}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\alpha,i}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive particle flux of
neutral state $\alpha$ along resolved transport direction $i$,
$D_{\alpha,i}$ is the corresponding neutral-state particle diffusivity
component, $n_\alpha$ is the number density of that neutral state, and $x_i$
is the coordinate along the resolved transport direction. The minus sign
defines down-gradient diffusive transport for a positive coefficient.

This parent quantity selects a specified neutral state and does not
aggregate over different neutral states, but it does not specify a transport
direction or microscopic mechanism. Direction-specific instances include
[poloidal neutral-state particle
diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_state_particle_diffusivity).

items.name: toroidal_ion_torque_density
items.description:
Local toroidal torque density on all ion species and charge states, giving
the external source rate of ion angular momentum about the symmetry axis
with its major-radius moment arm.
items.documentation:
The toroidal ion torque density is the local rate at which external
processes change the angular momentum of the combined ion population about
the symmetry axis. It is the toroidal component of the parent [ion torque
density](name:ion_torque_density), summed over ion species and charge
states; internal ion–ion exchanges cancel in this aggregate.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, it is defined from the
net external ion force density by

$$
\tau_{\phi,i} = R f_{\phi,i} = R\,\mathbf{f}_i \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\tau_{\phi,i}$ is the toroidal ion torque density, $R$ is major
radius in m, $\mathbf{f}_i$ is the external force density on the combined
ion population in N m$^{-3}$, $f_{\phi,i}$ is its toroidal component, and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal
angle. Unlike the broader [toroidal torque
density](name:toroidal_torque_density), this quantity is restricted to the
ion population.

Sign convention: Positive when the external torque increases ion angular
momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: current_of_passive_loop
items.description:
Signed conventional electric current circulating in one axisymmetric passive
conducting loop, induced by changing linked magnetic flux and
electromagnetic coupling.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the conventional electric current circulating in a single
passive conducting loop. It represents the electromagnetically induced
response of the passive conductor to changing linked magnetic flux,
including transients caused by changing plasma currents, active-coil
currents, disruptions, and coupling to other conductors.

For a passive loop with no separately applied circuit voltage, the linear
circuit response is represented by

$$
\mathcal{R} I(t) + L\frac{dI(t)}{dt} = -\frac{d\Phi_{\rm ext}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $I(t)$ is the loop current, $\mathcal{R}$ is the loop resistance, $L$
is its self-inductance, $t$ is time, and $\Phi_{\rm ext}(t)$ is the
externally linked magnetic flux, including mutual coupling and excluding
flux generated by the loop's own current. The negative sign expresses Lenz's
law.

The quantity applies to one passive conducting loop and denotes its net
circuit current, with all induced contributions aggregated into that loop
current. It excludes current imposed by an external power supply and is
distinct from the current carried by the plasma or by an actively driven
coil. The loop-resolved current contributes to the net [current of a passive
structure](name:current_of_passive_structure) when multiple passive
conducting elements form one structure.

The magnetic coupling and orientation of the loop are interpreted
consistently with its [effective turn
count](name:effective_turn_count_of_passive_loop), whose sign represents the
element orientation relative to positive loop current.

Sign convention: Positive when conventional current circulates in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

items.name: toroidal_tritium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Signed toroidal fluid velocity of the tritium-ion population evaluated at
the magnetic axis and resolved in the direction of increasing toroidal
angle.
items.documentation:
The tritium-ion toroidal velocity is the density-weighted fluid-velocity
component of tritium ions evaluated at the magnetic axis, where the gradient
of poloidal magnetic flux vanishes. It describes collective ion motion
rather than thermal speed or individual-particle gyro-orbit velocity.

For all tritium ion charge states included in the species definition, the
quantity is

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{T}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{T}^{q+}}\,\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{T}^{q+}}\cdot\hat{\phi}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{T}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ is the ionic charge state, $n_{\mathrm{T}^{q+}}$ is its number
density, $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{T}^{q+}}$ is its fluid velocity, and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The corresponding local tritium abundance is given by
[tritium_density_at_magnetic_axis](name:tritium_density_at_magnetic_axis).

Sign convention: Positive when the tritium-ion velocity component points in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: safety_factor_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Safety factor at the magnetic axis is the signed toroidal-to-poloidal
field-line winding ratio at the innermost closed flux surface, the value
approached as nested closed magnetic flux surfaces contract toward the axis.
It gives the toroidal turns made by a magnetic field line per complete
poloidal circuit in that limit.
items.documentation:
Safety factor at magnetic axis

On each neighboring nested closed magnetic flux surface, the [safety
factor](name:safety_factor) is defined by

$$
q = \frac{1}{2\pi}\oint \frac{\mathbf{B}\cdot\nabla\phi}{\mathbf{B}\cdot\nabla\theta}\,d\theta
$$

where $q$ is the safety factor, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $\nabla$
is the spatial gradient operator, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, and $\theta$
is the poloidal angle; the integral follows a magnetic field line through
one complete poloidal circuit. The toroidal angle $\phi$ belongs to the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $Z$
is vertical height, and $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed from
above.

This quantity is the value of $q$ at the innermost closed flux surface:
writing $q_{\mathrm{axis}}$ for it,
$q_{\mathrm{axis}}=\lim_{\mathcal{S}\to\mathrm{axis}} q(\mathcal{S})$, where
$\mathcal{S}$ ranges over the nested closed magnetic flux surfaces
contracting toward the magnetic axis and $q(\mathcal{S})$ is the safety
factor on $\mathcal{S}$. It is a single signed equilibrium winding value
with no species, population, or charge-state aggregation. It is a limit from
neighboring closed surfaces, not a direct evaluation of the winding
integrand on the axis, not a value on a finite-radius surface, not a volume
average, and not a local ratio of magnetic-field component magnitudes.
Proximity of this value to low-order rational numbers indicates
susceptibility to core-resonant magnetohydrodynamic modes such as sawteeth.

It is the magnetic-axis specialization of the [safety
factor](name:safety_factor), which describes field-line winding as a
function of flux-surface label. The [minimum safety
factor](name:minimum_safety_factor) instead selects the closed surface where
the safety-factor magnitude is smallest, and the [safety factor at the
plasma boundary](name:safety_factor_at_plasma_boundary) is the confined-side
outer-boundary value. The [rotational transform](name:rotational_transform)
is the reciprocal winding ratio, $\iota = 1/q$, where $\iota$ is the signed
number of poloidal turns per toroidal turn.

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal angle advance of a magnetic
field line is in the direction of increasing $\phi$ as the poloidal angle
$\theta$ increases.

The closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux
surfaces are arranged. Where $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}},
Z_{\mathrm{axis}}) = 0$, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is poloidal magnetic
field; $R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the O-point inside the
nested closed flux surfaces.

items.name: parallel_fast_particle_pressure
items.description:
Parallel fast-particle pressure measures the field-aligned kinetic stress of
a specified suprathermal population, including random and directed particle
motion.
items.documentation:
The parallel fast-particle pressure is the field-aligned component of the
kinetic stress carried by a specified suprathermal particle distribution.
Together with the perpendicular component, it characterizes pressure
anisotropy relative to the local magnetic field.

For a nonrelativistic species, the defining second velocity moment is:

$$
p_{\parallel,s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = m_s \int v_\parallel^2 f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{\parallel,s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the parallel fast-particle pressure
of species $s$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $m_s$ is the particle mass,
$f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle distribution function,
$\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume
element. The parallel velocity is $v_\parallel=\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{b}$,
where $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local
magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

Only the suprathermal population represented by the specified distribution
contributes; thermal-particle pressure is excluded. The quantity is not
restricted to ions and does not imply an all-species or all-charge-state
total. The velocity moment is not centered on the fast-particle mean flow,
so directed parallel motion contributes in addition to random motion.

For the same population and spatial averaging, the [fast-particle
pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure) is the trace pressure
$p_{s,\mathrm{fast}}=(p_{\parallel,s,\mathrm{fast}}+2p_{\perp,s,\mathrm{fast}})/3$,
where $p_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ denotes the isotropic trace pressure and
$p_{\perp,s,\mathrm{fast}}$ denotes the [perpendicular fast-particle
pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure), the transverse kinetic
stress per perpendicular degree of freedom. Parallel and perpendicular
pressures need not be equal.

items.name: radial_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity
items.description:
Radial current density due to parallel viscosity is the signed major-radius
projection of the electric current contribution associated with
magnetic-field-aligned viscous stress.
items.documentation:
Radial current density due to parallel viscosity is the signed local
projection of the current contribution associated with the divergence of
parallel viscous stress onto the major-radius direction. Parallel identifies
the viscous-stress mechanism, not the direction of the current.

The defining projection is:

$$
j_R^{(\mathrm{pv})} = \mathbf{j}^{(\mathrm{pv})}\cdot\hat{R}
$$

where $j_R^{(\mathrm{pv})}$ is the radial current-density contribution,
$\mathbf{j}^{(\mathrm{pv})}$ is the full [current-density vector due to
parallel viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity), and
$\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius. In the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is distance from the
toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height. The superscript $\mathrm{pv}$ identifies the parallel-viscosity
contribution.

In the magnetized edge plasma, this is a local, mechanism-resolved
contribution to [current density](name:current_density), not the total
radial current density or a flux-surface average. It excludes the
perpendicular-viscosity contribution. The major-radius direction is not
generally the flux-surface-normal direction or a direction perpendicular to
the magnetic field.

Parallel viscosity does not require its full current-density contribution to
be field aligned. The [parallel current density due to parallel
viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) is the
magnetic-field-aligned projection of the same parent vector, rather than its
major-radius projection.

Sign convention: Positive when the parallel-viscosity current-density
contribution points toward increasing major radius, away from the toroidal
symmetry axis.

items.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part
items.description:
Real part of the poloidal perturbed plasma velocity is the in-phase
component of the complex first-order plasma-velocity amplitude for toroidal
mode number n, resolved tangent to increasing poloidal angle in the
flux-coordinate basis (ρ, θ, φ). The toroidal angle φ is that of the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame; equilibrium flow and the
quadrature component are excluded.
items.documentation:
Real part of the poloidal perturbed plasma velocity is the in-phase
component of the complex first-order plasma-velocity perturbation amplitude
for one toroidal Fourier harmonic with mode number $n$. The poloidal
component is resolved along the local basis direction tangent to increasing
poloidal angle $\theta$ in a specified flux-coordinate basis
$(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, with $\phi$ the toroidal angle of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius, $Z$ is vertical
height, and $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed from above
$+\hat{Z}$. It is distinct from equilibrium plasma flow.

For a complex poloidal amplitude in that flux-coordinate basis, the real
part is defined by:

$$
v_{\theta,1}^{\mathrm{Re}}(\rho,\theta;n) = \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\tilde{v}_{\theta,1}(\rho,\theta;n)\right]
$$

where $v_{\theta,1}^{\mathrm{Re}}$ is this real poloidal perturbation
amplitude, $\tilde{v}_{\theta,1}$ is the [poloidal perturbed plasma
velocity](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity), $\tilde{\mathbf{v}}_1$
is the complex first-order plasma-velocity perturbation eigenfunction for
harmonic $n$, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$ is the local normalized direction
tangent to increasing $\theta$ with
$\tilde{v}_{\theta,1}=\tilde{\mathbf{v}}_1\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$,
$\rho$ is the radial flux label, and $n$ is the toroidal Fourier mode
number.

Together with [poloidal perturbed plasma velocity imaginary
part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_imaginary_part), this quantity
specifies the complex poloidal velocity amplitude for the selected harmonic.
It is not the full real-space poloidal velocity at a particular toroidal
angle; the dependence on $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame is supplied by the chosen Fourier harmonic convention. Multiplication
of the complex eigenfunction by a constant phase factor changes the split
between real and imaginary parts without changing the underlying linear
mode, so a fixed phase reference is required for this real component.

Sign convention: Positive when the real first-order velocity perturbation
component projects along $+\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$, the local direction of
increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux-coordinate basis
$(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, after the complex eigenmode phase reference is fixed.

items.name: neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion
items.description:
Global neutron production rate from thermonuclear reactions among Maxwellian
bulk ions, applicable to individual neutron-producing reaction channels or
their aggregate total, excluding fast-ion fusion contributions.
items.documentation:
The neutron source rate due to thermal fusion is the global rate at which
neutrons are generated by thermonuclear reactions between plasma ion species
whose velocity distributions are Maxwellian. It encompasses both per-channel
rates for a single neutron-producing reaction (DD, DT, or TT) and the
aggregate sum over all channels, and is an instance of the general
[source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion](name:source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion)
restricted to the neutron product.

For each neutron-producing reaction channel $c$ between reactant species $a$
and $b$, the channel source rate is:

$$
S_{n,c}^{\rm th} = \frac{1}{1 + \delta_{ab}} \int n_a \, n_b \, \langle \sigma v \rangle_c \, dV
$$

where $n_a$ and $n_b$ are the number densities of the two reactant species,
$\langle \sigma v \rangle_c$ is the Maxwell-averaged reaction-rate
coefficient for channel $c$, $\delta_{ab} = 1$ when the two reactants are
identical (as in DD and TT channels) and 0 otherwise, and the integral
extends over the confined plasma volume. The aggregate quantity sums
contributions from all neutron-producing channels.

This quantity excludes neutrons from beam-target fusion (see
flux_due_to_beam_thermal_fusion), beam-beam fusion, fusion-product
reactivation, and radio-frequency-tail ion populations. Per-channel
instances include
deuterium_deuterium_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion and
tritium_tritium_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion; the
channel-summed total is
[total_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion](name:total_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion).

items.name: neutral_internal_state_source_rate
items.description:
Neutral internal-state source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric
rate at which particles enter or leave one specified internal state of a
neutral species.
items.documentation:
Neutral internal-state source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric
rate at which particles enter or leave one specified internal state of a
neutral species. It supplies the source term in that state's particle-number
density transport equation, separately from spatial transport by particle
flux.

The net rate is defined by

$$
S_{0,a}(\psi)=\left\langle S_{0,a}^{\mathrm{gain}}-S_{0,a}^{\mathrm{loss}}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $S_{0,a}$ is the neutral internal-state source rate,
$S_{0,a}^{\mathrm{gain}}$ and $S_{0,a}^{\mathrm{loss}}$ are the local
volumetric rates of particle addition and removal, respectively, $0$ denotes
electrically neutral particles, $a$ identifies the specified internal state,
$\psi$ labels a magnetic flux surface, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$
denotes a flux-surface average.

This quantity applies to one neutral species and one internal energy or
excitation state, not to a nonzero ionic charge state. It is averaged over
each magnetic flux surface but is not summed over internal states or neutral
species. Positive values indicate net particle gain in the selected state;
negative values indicate net loss. It describes particle number, not
internal-energy transfer or particle flow through a surface.

Summing over all internal states of the same neutral species gives the
aggregate [neutral source rate](name:neutral_source_rate): $S_0=\sum_a
S_{0,a}$, where $S_0$ is that species' aggregate source rate. Transfers
between internal states contribute oppositely to the participating state
source rates and cancel in this sum.

items.name: incident_ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
items.description:
Incident ion energy flux at the wall due to recombination is the energy
delivered per unit wall area by ions that strike the wall and recombine
there. It is summed over ion species and charge states and excludes
kinetic-energy flux and emitted-particle contributions.
items.documentation:
Incident ion energy flux at the wall due to recombination is the
wall-directed energy transfer associated with ions that arrive at a material
wall and recombine there. It represents the recombination-energy channel
only, not the ions' translational kinetic-energy flux or other wall
energy-transfer mechanisms.

The quantity is defined as the species- and charge-state-summed
recombination-energy flux of incident ions:

$$
q_{\mathrm{rec},i}^{\mathrm{inc}} = \sum_s \sum_Z \Gamma_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{inc}} \, \epsilon_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{rec}}
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{rec},i}^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident ion energy flux at
the wall due to recombination, $s$ indexes ion species, $Z$ indexes charge
states, $\Gamma_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the particle flux of incident ions
of species $s$ and charge state $Z$ to the wall, and
$\epsilon_{s,Z}^{\mathrm{rec}}$ is the recombination energy delivered to the
wall per such incident ion.

The scope is local material wall surfaces and incident ions only. The
aggregation convention is summation over all ion species and all charge
states represented in the ion population. The quantity excludes neutral and
electron recombination-energy contributions, particles emitted from the
wall, kinetic-energy flux, radiation, and other non-recombination energy
channels.

Within the recombination energy-flux decomposition, this quantity is the
incident-ion component related to the [ion energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination). The
corresponding [energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) is the broader
recombination-channel quantity over the particle classes included in that
decomposition. These relationships are aggregations over species, charge
states, or particle classes; they do not define an incident-minus-emitted
net balance.

items.name: parallel_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia
items.description:
Parallel current density due to ion inertia is the signed projection of the
electric current produced by ion-fluid inertial acceleration along the local
magnetic field.
items.documentation:
Parallel current density due to ion inertia resolves the electric-current
contribution from ion-fluid inertial acceleration along the local magnetic
field. It represents a finite-ion-mass contribution rather than the total
current along the field.

The component is defined by directional projection:

$$
j_{\parallel} = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{inertia}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $j_{\parallel}$ is the parallel ion-inertia current-density component,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{inertia}}$ is the [current density due to ion
inertia](name:current_density_due_to_ion_inertia), and $\hat{\mathbf{b}} =
\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field.
Here, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its
magnitude, which must be nonzero for this projection to be defined.

This quantity is a local, mechanism-specific projection of [current
density](name:current_density), not the complete ion-inertia current vector,
its magnitude, or a spatially averaged current. It is distinct from the
total [parallel ion current density](name:parallel_ion_current_density),
which includes ion charge transport without restriction to the inertial
contribution. Unlike the [diamagnetic component due to ion
inertia](name:diamagnetic_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia), it resolves
current along the magnetic field rather than along a perpendicular
direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the ion-inertia current flows along the local
magnetic-field direction.

items.name: total_ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Charge-state-summed number density of all ion species at the internal
transport barrier, excluding neutral particles and charge weighting.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the total local number density of all included ion
populations evaluated at the flux-surface location assigned to the internal
transport barrier. It is the aggregate specialization of
ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier, rather than the density of a
selected species or charge state.

The total ion density is defined by

$$
n_{i,\mathrm{total}} = \sum_s \sum_Z n_{s,Z}
$$

where $n_{s,Z}$ is the number density of ion species $s$ in charge state
$Z$, and both sums include every ion population in the defined ion
inventory. The summation counts particles without weighting by ionic charge;
neutral particles are excluded. This convention distinguishes the quantity
from charge-weighted descriptors such as
charge_at_internal_transport_barrier.

items.name: poloidal_momentum_flux
items.description:
Poloidal momentum flux is the signed rate per unit area at which the
poloidal component of linear momentum crosses an oriented surface.
items.documentation:
Poloidal momentum flux is the poloidal component of the linear-momentum
transfer across an oriented surface per unit area and time. The poloidal
qualifier identifies the transported momentum component, while the surface
normal identifies the transport direction.

The component is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm p} = \hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Gamma} = \hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}\cdot\mathsf{T}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm p}$ is the poloidal momentum flux, $\hat{\mathbf
e}_{\mathrm p}$ is the positive poloidal unit vector, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}$
is the [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux) across the oriented surface,
$\mathsf{T}$ is the linear-momentum-flux tensor, and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is
the chosen surface-normal unit vector. The poloidal direction lies in a
constant-$\phi$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

This quantity applies to a selected ion or neutral population, or to a
combined population whose constituent momentum fluxes are summed. Unlike
[poloidal ion momentum flux](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux), it does not
specify an ion carrier. It includes convective transport, pressure, and
viscous or turbulent stress contributions rather than only diffusive
transport. It is a transport rate of [momentum](name:momentum), not momentum
itself, and implies neither transport along the poloidal tangent nor
flux-surface averaging.

Sign convention: Positive when the net transfer across the chosen surface
normal carries clockwise poloidal momentum, viewed around the magnetic axis
in the poloidal plane with the machine symmetry axis to the left and
increasing $Z$ upward.

items.name: power_due_to_line_radiation
items.description:
Total electromagnetic power emitted in discrete spectral lines by
bound-bound transitions of plasma atoms and ions.
items.documentation:
Line-radiation power is the volume-integrated electromagnetic emission from
bound-bound transitions of atomic and ionic populations in the plasma. It
represents the energy carried by discrete spectral lines and is a radiative
loss from the emitting plasma.

For downward transitions, the emitted power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{line}} = \int_V \sum_s \sum_{i>j} n_{s,i} A_{s,ij} h\nu_{s,ij}\,dV
$$

where $V$ is the emitting plasma volume, $n_{s,i}$ is the population density
of upper state $i$ of species $s$ in m$^{-3}$, $A_{s,ij}$ is the transition
probability in s$^{-1}$, $h$ is Planck's constant, and $\nu_{s,ij}$ is the
emitted-photon frequency in s$^{-1}$. The sums include all specified atomic
and ionic emitters and radiative transitions.

This quantity includes line emission from hydrogenic and impurity species,
but excludes continuum bremsstrahlung represented by
[bremsstrahlung_power](name:bremsstrahlung_power) and other channels such as
[power_due_to_synchrotron_radiation](name:power_due_to_synchrotron_radiation).
It contributes to
[total_plasma_radiated_power](name:total_plasma_radiated_power), while
power_due_to_impurity_radiation covers the impurity-specific component.

items.name: toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk velocity of helium-4 ions, evaluated on the
flux surface identified with the internal transport barrier.
items.documentation:
The toroidal helium-4 velocity is the density-weighted bulk-flow component
of helium-4 ions, evaluated on the flux surface identified with the internal
transport barrier. It includes helium-4 ions across their ionization charge
states and excludes neutral helium-4.

$$
v_{\phi,4}=\frac{\sum_z n_{4,z}v_{\phi,4,z}}{\sum_z n_{4,z}}
$$

where $v_{\phi,4}$ is the charge-state-averaged helium-4 toroidal velocity,
$n_{4,z}$ is the helium-4 ion number density in charge state $z$, and
$v_{\phi,4,z}$ is that charge state's toroidal velocity in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The toroidal component is projected along
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ and is distinct from the
flux-surface-averaged quantity at the plasma boundary and from the analogous
[toroidal helium-3
velocity](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier).

Sign convention: Positive when the helium-4 ion flow has a component in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Toroidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary is the net flux of toroidal
magnetic field through the poloidal cross-section enclosed by the plasma
boundary, including externally imposed and plasma-poloidal-current
contributions.
items.documentation:
Toroidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary is the net flux of the
toroidal magnetic-field component through the poloidal cross-section
enclosed by the plasma boundary. It is the boundary value of toroidal
magnetic flux used to define toroidal-flux radial labels.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed
from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height, the boundary toroidal
flux is defined by

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},b} = \int_{\Omega_b} \mathbf{B}\cdot\hat{\phi}\, dA_{RZ} = \int_{\Omega_b} B_\phi(R,Z)\, dA_{RZ} = \int_{\Omega_b} \frac{F(\psi(R,Z))}{R}\, dA_{RZ}
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},b}$ is this boundary toroidal flux, $\Omega_b$ is
the boundary-enclosed region in the poloidal plane of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field,
$B_\phi$ is its toroidal component in tesla, $dA_{RZ}$ is the poloidal
cross-sectional area element in square meters, $F(\psi)=R B_\phi$ is the
poloidal-current function in tesla meters, and $\psi$ is the equilibrium
poloidal magnetic-flux label.

The geometric measure of $\Omega_b$ is the [poloidal cross-sectional area of
the plasma
boundary](name:poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_plasma_boundary).
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor},b}$ includes both externally imposed toroidal-field flux
and the contribution associated with plasma poloidal current, and is
distinct from [toroidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary due to poloidal
current](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary_due_to_poloidal_current),
which contains only that plasma-current contribution. It also differs from
[poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma
boundary](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary), which is magnetic
flux through a horizontal disk rather than through the boundary-enclosed
poloidal cross-section.

Sign convention: Positive when the net toroidal magnetic field threading the
plasma-boundary poloidal cross-section points in the direction of increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: poloidal_ion_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Effective particle transport coefficient relating an ion species’ poloidal
diffusive flux to the opposing poloidal gradient of its number density
summed over ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
The poloidal ion diffusion coefficient characterizes local Fickian particle
diffusion of a specified ion species along the poloidal tangent. It
describes the poloidal-poloidal diagonal response rather than a
direction-independent diffusivity or a particular microscopic transport
mechanism.

In flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, $\rho$ labels magnetic flux
surfaces, $\theta$ is the poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle.
Retaining only the poloidal density-gradient contribution, the defining
relation is:

$$
\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,\mathrm{p}}\,\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}\cdot\nabla n_i
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal diffusive ion
particle flux density contributed by that gradient, $D_{i,\mathrm{p}}$ is
the poloidal ion diffusion coefficient, $n_i$ is the ion species’ number
density, $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the unit tangent toward
increasing $\theta$ at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$, and $\nabla$ denotes the
spatial gradient. The minus sign expresses down-gradient transport for
positive diffusivity.

The density and particle flux are summed over all ionic charge states of the
specified species, excluding neutrals and other ion species. The coefficient
describes the effective flux-gradient response of this aggregate; it is not
a sum of charge-state diffusion coefficients. In contrast, the [poloidal ion
charge-state diffusion
coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) applies
to one specified ionic charge state.

This is the poloidal-poloidal diagonal specialization of the
particle-diffusion response associated with the direction-unspecified [ion
diffusion coefficient](name:ion_diffusion_coefficient). It excludes
convective particle flux and ion energy or momentum diffusion, is not a sum
of directional coefficients, and does not encode off-diagonal tensor
couplings. Consequently, the displayed relation represents the complete
poloidal diffusive flux only when contributions from other gradient
directions vanish or are neglected.

items.name: parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate
items.description:
Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional or neoclassical decay of
magnetic-field-aligned bulk-flow momentum in an ion species, including all
its ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
The parallel ion momentum damping rate is the effective inverse relaxation
time for collisional or neoclassical relaxation of an ion species' ordered
flow along the local magnetic field. It describes damping of the
field-aligned momentum component, not the direction of momentum transport.

In a local linear damping closure, the damping contribution to the momentum
balance is:

$$
\left(\frac{\partial g_{i,\parallel}}{\partial t}\right)_{\mathrm{damp}} = -\nu_{i,\parallel}g_{i,\parallel}
$$

where $g_{i,\parallel}$ is the ion species' parallel momentum density,
$\nu_{i,\parallel}$ is this damping rate, and $t$ is time. The index $i$
identifies the ion species, $\parallel$ denotes the field-aligned
projection, and the subscript $\mathrm{damp}$ selects only the damping
contribution. For a constant positive rate with no other terms acting, its
reciprocal is the exponential relaxation time.

The species momentum density is summed over all ionic charge states, and the
corresponding bulk-flow velocity is the density-weighted mean over all ionic
charge states. This effective species-level coefficient is not a sum of
charge-state damping rates; the [parallel ion charge-state momentum damping
rate](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate) instead
describes one specified charge state. Diffusive and convective momentum
fluxes and externally applied momentum sources are excluded from this
damping term.

This quantity is the field-aligned entry of the [ion momentum damping
rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate), whose directional entries describe
anisotropic relaxation of ordered ion [momentum](name:momentum). The damping
