coefficient is nonnegative for dissipative relaxation and does not inherit
the sign of the parallel flow.

items.name: launched_pulse_energy_of_thomson_scattering_laser
items.description:
Optical energy carried by one Thomson-scattering laser pulse immediately
before it enters the vacuum vessel, before interaction with the plasma.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the optical energy carried by one Thomson-scattering
probing laser pulse at the vessel entrance, before the pulse interacts with
the plasma.

The pulse energy is defined by integrating the instantaneous laser power
over the pulse duration:

$$
E_{\rm pulse} = \int_{t_0}^{t_1} P_{\rm laser}(t)\,dt
$$

where $E_{\rm pulse}$ is the pulse energy, $P_{\rm laser}(t)$ is the
instantaneous optical power at the vessel entrance, and $t_0$ and $t_1$ are
the pulse start and end times.

The quantity applies to a single probing-laser pulse immediately before
vessel entry. It is an energy aggregation over that pulse only, not a sum
over multiple pulses or a time-integrated laser train.

It excludes energy lost after vessel entry, energy remaining after plasma
crossing, scattered optical energy, and laser-system energy not carried by
the incident pulse.

The incident pulse energy provides the normalization for absolute
interpretation of Thomson-scattered signal intensity. It is distinct from
the wavelength-dependent response described by the [spectral efficiency of
the Thomson-scattering
detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_thomson_scattering_detector).

items.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum transfer rate per
plasma volume delivered to a specified thermal ion charge state through
Coulomb collisions.
items.documentation:
Collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum source associated
with Coulomb momentum transfer to a specified thermal ion charge state.
Orbit classes and directional components select particular contributions
without changing this common physical meaning.

For a selected angular-momentum direction, the torque density is defined by

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a} = (\mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_a
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{coll},a}$ is the torque density about direction $a$,
$\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the rotation axis,
$\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional force density transferred to
the specified charge state, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_a$ is the corresponding
unit vector. For toroidal angular momentum in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, this relation reduces to $R f_\phi$.

This quantity is the charge-state-resolved realization of ion charge-state
torque density due to collisions; [co-passing thermal ion charge-state
torque density due to
collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
is one orbit-resolved instance.

Sign convention: Positive when the selected angular-momentum transfer is in
the positive orientation of its stated axis; for toroidal angular momentum,
positive is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description:
Signed projection along the toroidal symmetry axis of the mass- and
charge-independent E×B guiding-center drift for one specified ion charge
state in the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
The vertical component of the [ion charge-state E×B drift
velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is its
signed projection along the toroidal symmetry axis. This direction is the
vertical direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For the ideal E×B guiding-center drift, the defining projection is

$$
v_{E,Z} = \mathbf{v}_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}.
$$

Here $v_{E,Z}$ is the vertical drift component for the specified ion charge
state, $\mathbf{v}_E$ is its E×B guiding-center drift velocity, $\mathbf{E}$
is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field, and
$\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the symmetry axis toward
increasing vertical height. The definition requires a nonzero magnetic field
and magnetized ions.

This quantity applies locally to one specified charge state of one ion
species in the edge plasma, including the scrape-off layer; it is neither
summed nor averaged over charge states or species. The ideal drift is
independent of ion mass and charge and is perpendicular to both local
fields. Other contributions to ion motion are excluded. This is a signed
velocity component, not a vertical position or the magnitude of the drift
velocity.

Together with the [radial
component](name:radial_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) and
[toroidal
component](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift),
it resolves the parent drift vector in the cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
The vertical component need not vanish because the symmetry axis is not
generally aligned with the local magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when the E×B guiding-center drift has a component
toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: trapped_torque_density
items.description:
Net angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume for magnetically trapped
particles, retaining the complete torque-vector direction.
items.documentation:
Torque density for magnetically trapped particles is the net
angular-momentum transfer rate to the trapped-particle population per unit
volume. It retains the complete torque-vector direction rather than
selecting a toroidal component or combining the trapped contribution with
passing-particle contributions.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{trap}} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0} \frac{1}{\Delta V}\frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{trap}}}{dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{trap}}$ is the torque-density vector for
magnetically trapped particles, $\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{trap}}$ is the
angular momentum transferred to the magnetically trapped population, $\Delta
V$ is a volume element, and $t$ is time.

This is the trapped-particle contribution to the broader [torque
density](name:torque_density); it excludes co-passing, counter-passing, and
population-unresolved torque contributions. The [toroidal trapped torque
density](name:toroidal_trapped_torque_density) is its toroidal component.

Sign convention: Positive when each resolved component points along the
corresponding positive unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical
$(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ basis, with
$\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$.

items.name: neutral_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description:
Volume-averaged thermal pressure of neutral atoms and molecules in the
scrape-off layer, the open-field-line region between the last closed flux
surface and material plasma-facing components.
items.documentation:
Neutral pressure over the scrape-off layer is the volume-averaged thermal
pressure of neutral atoms and molecules in the open-field-line region
between the last closed flux surface and the material plasma-facing
components. It represents the neutral-gas contribution to the SOL pressure,
distinct from the electron partial pressure described by [electron pressure
over the scrape-off layer](name:electron_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer),
and is a component of [pressure over the scrape-off
layer](name:pressure_over_scrape_off_layer).

The defining volume average is

$$
\overline{p}_{\mathrm{n,SOL}} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{SOL}}} \int_{\mathrm{SOL}} p_{\mathrm{n}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V, \qquad p_{\mathrm{n}}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_s n_s(\mathbf{r}) k_B T_s(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{SOL}}$ is the scrape-off-layer volume, $\mathbf{r}$ is
position, $p_{\mathrm{n}}$ is local neutral pressure, $s$ indexes neutral
atomic and molecular species, $n_s$ is their number density, $T_s$ is their
thermodynamic temperature, and $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant.

The quantity excludes charged-particle pressure and represents an average
over the entire scrape-off-layer domain rather than a pressure evaluated at
a particular location.

items.name: total_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion
items.description:
Total neutron production rate from thermonuclear neutron-producing
deuterium-deuterium, deuterium-tritium, and tritium-tritium reaction
branches among Maxwellian bulk ions, excluding beam-target and beam-beam
fast-ion contributions.
items.documentation:
The total neutron source rate due to thermal fusion is the number of
neutrons produced per unit time by the neutron-producing thermal
deuterium-deuterium, deuterium-tritium, and tritium-tritium reaction
branches between bulk ions with locally Maxwellian velocity distributions.
It is the channel-summed member of [neutron source rate due to thermal
fusion](name:neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion), equal to the sum of
deuterium-deuterium neutron source rate due to thermal fusion,
deuterium-tritium neutron source rate due to thermal fusion, and
[tritium-tritium neutron source rate due to thermal
fusion](name:tritium_tritium_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion).

The channel-summed thermal neutron source rate is defined by

$$
S_{n,\mathrm{tot}}^{\mathrm{th}} = \int_V \sum_{c \in \{DD,DT,TT\}} \nu_{n,c}\,\frac{n_{a_c} n_{b_c}}{1+\delta_{a_c b_c}}\,\langle\sigma v\rangle_c(T_{a_c},T_{b_c})\,dV
$$

where $S_{n,\mathrm{tot}}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the total source rate, $V$ is
the emitting plasma volume, $c$ labels a neutron-producing thermal fusion
branch, $\nu_{n,c}$ is the neutron multiplicity of branch $c$, $a_c$ and
$b_c$ are its reactant ion species, $n_{a_c}$ and $n_{b_c}$ are their local
bulk number densities, $\delta_{a_c b_c}$ is one for identical reactants and
zero otherwise, $\langle\sigma v\rangle_c$ is the Maxwellian-averaged
reactivity, $T_{a_c}$ and $T_{b_c}$ are the local reactant temperatures, and
$dV$ is a volume element. The denominator prevents double counting of
identical reactant pairs.

Only reactions among locally Maxwellian bulk ions are included; beam-target,
beam-beam, fusion-product, and other nonthermal fast-ion contributions are
excluded. For deuterium-deuterium fusion, only the D(d,n)$^3\mathrm{He}$
neutron branch contributes; the D(d,p)T proton branch is not counted. For
deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium neutron branches $\nu_{n,c}=1$,
while for tritium-tritium fusion $\nu_{n,c}=2$.

items.name: minor_length_of_iron_core_segment
items.description:
Minor length of an iron-core segment is the non-negative Euclidean length of
the beta-side of the segment's oblique poloidal cross-section in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. The beta-side is inclined with
respect to the height axis Z and defines the segment's extent along that
side.
items.documentation:
Minor length of an iron-core segment is the non-negative Euclidean length of
the $\beta$-side of the segment's oblique poloidal cross-section in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The $\beta$-side is
the side whose direction in that poloidal cross-section is inclined by the
angle $\beta$ with respect to the height axis $Z$.

This quantity applies to the geometric cross-section of one iron-core
segment. Its aggregation convention is none: it is a single side length for
the specified segment. It is not the toroidal extent, material volume, or
any magnetic property of the iron core.

It is the $\beta$-side counterpart of the [major length of an iron-core
segment](name:major_length_of_iron_core_segment), which refers to the other
oblique side length. Together with the corresponding inclination angles,
these side lengths define the size of the segment's oblique poloidal
cross-section.

items.name: wavelength_of_visible_camera
items.description:
Wavelength specifying either the short-wavelength or long-wavelength edge of
a photon-detection response interval.
items.documentation:
A response-band boundary wavelength is the spectral location of one edge of
an optical detector's photon-sensitivity interval. It identifies where the
accepted response range begins or ends, rather than describing the response
magnitude within that range.

The wavelength is related to the corresponding electromagnetic frequency by

$$
\lambda_{\mathrm{edge}} = \frac{c}{\nu_{\mathrm{edge}}}
$$

where $\lambda_{\mathrm{edge}}$ is the boundary wavelength, $c$ is the speed
of light in vacuum, and $\nu_{\mathrm{edge}}$ is the electromagnetic
frequency at that boundary.

This quantity applies to either endpoint of a photon-detection response
interval: the lower endpoint is represented by [lower-bound wavelength of a
visible camera](name:lower_bound_wavelength_of_visible_camera), and the
upper endpoint by [upper-bound wavelength of a visible
camera](name:upper_bound_wavelength_of_visible_camera). It is an endpoint
value, not a spectral average, integrated response, or response-equivalent
width.

The two boundary wavelengths delimit the admitted spectral interval; the
lower-wavelength boundary precedes the upper-wavelength boundary. This
distinguishes each boundary from [effective spectral width of a spectrometer
channel](name:effective_spectral_width_of_spectrometer_channel), which
characterizes the extent of a response rather than one endpoint, and from
the general wavelength quantity, which need not be associated with a
response-band boundary.

items.name: neutral_temperature
items.description:
Temperature of a neutral species measures random translational kinetic
energy per particle relative to the population's mean flow.
items.documentation:
Temperature of a neutral species characterizes the energy of random
translational motion relative to that population's mean flow. It applies to
neutral atoms or molecules and excludes directed-flow energy and internal
excitation energy.

A cold or hot neutral temperature is that of the named component alone;
without the component it covers the whole neutral population of the selected
species.

The underlying kinetic definition is

$$
\frac{3}{2}T_0 = \left\langle \frac{1}{2}m_0\left|\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_0\right|^2\right\rangle
$$

where $T_0$ is the neutral translational temperature expressed as an energy,
$m_0$ is the particle mass of the specified neutral species, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, and $\mathbf{u}_0$ is the [mean neutral
velocity](name:neutral_velocity). The angle brackets denote a
particle-number-weighted average over the selected neutral population. This
second-moment definition remains applicable to a non-Maxwellian
distribution.

The species-level aggregation convention is the density-weighted mean over
all charge states, not a sum of state temperatures. Since the particles here
are neutral, only the zero-charge state contributes; ion temperatures are
excluded. No particular plasma region, cold or hot population, or internal
state is selected by the unqualified quantity.

The [cold-neutral temperature](name:cold_neutral_temperature) and
[hot-neutral temperature](name:hot_neutral_temperature_at_plasma_boundary)
restrict this definition to their respective populations. The [neutral
internal-state temperature](name:neutral_internal_state_temperature) applies
the same translational definition to particles in one specified internal
state; it is not an internal excitation temperature. The [volume-averaged
neutral temperature](name:volume_averaged_neutral_temperature) is a spatial
average of this quantity rather than its value at an individual location.

items.name: height_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description:
Height of a poloidal field coil is the nonnegative full vertical extent of
the rectangular conductor cross-section of an individual active coil
element.
items.documentation:
Height of poloidal field coil

The height is the difference between the upper and lower vertical boundary
coordinates:

$$
h = Z_{\mathrm{upper}} - Z_{\mathrm{lower}}
$$

where $h$ is the full height, and $Z_{\mathrm{upper}}$ and
$Z_{\mathrm{lower}}$ are the vertical coordinates of the upper and lower
boundaries in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Here, $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when
viewed from above, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity applies to an individual active coil element's rectangular
conductor cross-section; it is not an aggregate over elements or coils. It
is the full dimension, not a half-height or the vertical position of the
cross-section center, and is distinct from the radial cross-sectional extent
represented by the [width of a poloidal field
coil](name:width_of_poloidal_field_coil).

For a rectangular cross-section, the height and width determine the [area of
a poloidal field coil](name:area_of_poloidal_field_coil) as $A = wh$, where
$A$ is the cross-sectional area, $w$ is the width, and $h$ is the height.
